Title: Indian national jailed for 19 years over plot to kill Sikh separatist in US
Article:
NEW YORK: An Indian man was sentenced Friday to more than 19 years in a US prison for plotting to hire a hitman to kill a Sikh separatist on American soil, allegedly on behalf of Indian intelligence.
The case strained ties between Washington and New Delhi, which denied any involvement in Nikhil Gupta's foiled ploy to assassinate dual US-Canadian citizen Gurpatwant Singh Pannun.
Gupta, 55, pleaded guilty in February to all three counts he faced: murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and conspiracy to commit money laundering.
"Today's sentence holds Gupta accountable for his cold and calculated plot," US Attorney Jamie McDonald said in a statement.
US federal prosecutors alleged that an Indian intelligence officer, who remains at large, directed the plot and recruited Gupta in May 2023 to hire a hitman to carry out the murder.
Pannun, the intended target, is affiliated with a New York-based group called Sikhs for Justice that advocates for the secession of Punjab, a northern Indian state with a large Sikh population.
He vowed to "continue pursuing Punjab's independence from Indian occupation" in remarks outside a Manhattan courthouse after sentencing.
"I'm ready to face India's bullet if that is the price I have to pay," Pannun said, also calling for the Indian intelligence official to face US justice.
Canada separately alleged in 2023 that India arranged a plot on its soil that ended in the killing of a Sikh separatist, who was a naturalized Canadian citizen.
Hardeep Singh Nijjar, 45, was shot dead by masked gunmen outside the Sikh temple he presided over after being wanted by Indian authorities for alleged terrorism offenses and conspiracy to commit murder – accusations he denied.
India dismissed Ottawa's allegations, which sent relations into freefall, with both nations expelling a slew of diplomats.--AFP

Title: Severe storm destroys thousands of homes, kills 3 in Brazil
Article:
BRASÍLIA: A powerful storm with winds exceeding 100km per hour killed three people and destroyed around 5,000 homes Friday in southern Brazil, as authorities raced to rescue injured survivors and find more casualties in the wreckage.
Rain and high winds battered Tupancireta early Friday, tearing up buildings and about 100 trees in the municipality that is home to 20,000 people.
"It's something never seen before, a movie scene," Tupancireta Mayor Gustavo Herter told local media.
"Our hospital was blocked by the trees around it, the access roads to the municipality were blocked with trees. The city is finished," he said. The hospital's roof was also destroyed and 11 patients had to be transferred.
The city was without electricity and water after the storm hit at around 3am and lasted less than an hour, Herter said.
Three people were found dead, according to the state government of Rio Grande do Sul, where Tupancireta is located.
Another 32 municipalities also reported damage.
President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva ordered emergency teams be sent to the region in response to the storm.
"We know there was a party in the municipality where the roof of that structure ended up collapsing," Luciano Boeira, state coordinator of civil defence, told Radio Gaucha.
Brazilian meteorologists said winds reached 114km per hour during the storm.
Civil defence described the storm as a "supercell," which often precedes a tornado with strong upward air currents, and has not ruled out the finding that a tornado hit the city.
State officials have allocated about US$330,000 in local currency to respond to the disaster.
Southern Brazil is frequently hit by tornados.-AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two workers drown after being sucked into water vortex at Bukit Tagar
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Two workers drowned after being sucked into a water vortex while cleaning a clogged drain at a rainwater retention pond at a cleaning services company in Bukit Tagar, Hulu Selangor.
The incident occurred about 11am on Wednesday, when the 27-year-old and 30-year-old men were believed to have become trapped inside an overflow chamber.
In a statement today, the Selangor Department of Occupational Safety and Health (JKKP) said preliminary investigations found that both victims were carrying out maintenance work and clearing rubbish clogging the overflow chamber of the pond.
"However, when the water passage was reopened, a powerful vortex formed, sucking them into the chamber where they became trapped by the force of the current.
"Another worker at the scene was rescued without sustaining any injuries," it said.
Following the incident, JKKP Selangor issued a Prohibition Notice against cleaning activities involving the clogged overflow chamber, as well as an Improvement Notice over the employer's failure to conduct a risk assessment for the work.
The department is also conducting further investigations, including summoning the employer and witnesses to record their statements.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Libyan man held over fatal Jalan Jelatek crash is private university student
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Libyan man involved in a fatal crash that killed a motorcyclist along Jalan Jelatek early today has been identified as a private university student.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department deputy chief Superintendent Suffian Abdullah confirmed that the 32-year-old driver also held a valid driving licence and passport.
"The car driver is a student at a private university in Bangi, Selangor, and holds a valid driving licence and passport," he said when contacted today.
Earlier, a 43-year-old motorcyclist was
killed after his motorcycle
was hit by a car driven by the Libyan at the Jalan Jelatek traffic light intersection at 1am.
Initial investigations showed the victim was riding from Taman Keramat towards Setiawangsa when the accident occured.
The car, travelling from Wangsa Maju, is believed to have run a red light before crashing into the motorcyclist.
The victim suffered severe injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene.
Alcohol and urine screening tests conducted on the car driver returned negative results.
The driver has been detained to assist in investigations, and a remand application against him will be made today.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for death by reckless or dangerous driving.

Title: Young protesters hit the streets across Europe
Article:
FRANKFURT: Protesters rallied across Europe on Friday to vent anger over issues from high living costs to military spending and the climate crisis, ramping up pressure on political leaders they accuse of ignoring the concerns of young people.
Demonstrators hit the streets in cities from Italy to Germany, Switzerland and Britain, many waving signs emblazoned with "fight for our future", setting off flares and burning cardboard models of tanks.
The rallies, coordinated by a youth-led coalition of over 50 groups, are fuelled by grievances that vary from place to place, including Israel's war in Gaza, high rents and deteriorating learning conditions at schools and universities.
But a common theme runs through them – a sense that governments across the continent are too busy with geopolitical crises and helping big business, and not investing enough in the well-being of younger generations.
Olivia Ferrario, an 18-year-old high school student at a protest in the Italian city of Milan, told AFP that young people were displaying their "dynamism and determination" by taking to the streets.
"If the government does not listen to us, we cannot remain silent," she said at the demonstration that attracted tens of thousands of protesters.
Police deployed in large numbers due to fears of a repeat of the street violence that has marred recent major protests in France and other countries.
- 'LOST SO MUCH HOPE' -
In Switzerland, organisers claimed that more than 40,000 protesters had taken to the streets nationwide.
"Austerity is social violence," read a banner in Lausanne, while another blared: "Be vegan, but eat the rich."
The demonstrations were mostly peaceful. But a small number of people clashed with police after it ended, resulting in the deployment of tear gas and water cannon, the domestic Keystone-ATS news agency reported.
In Berlin, about 1,000 university students and school pupils protested over concerns including Germany's rapid rearmament, which has stoked fears of a return to compulsory military service.
"I simply think it's indefensible... to force someone to learn how to fight and kill, and then send them to war," Helena Kossatz, 18, who finished high school last year, told AFP.
While Europe seeks to rearm in the face of a hostile Russia, organisers of the continent-wide protests say funds allocated to rearmament should be spent on education, youth policies and housing.
Several hundred protesters, some in school uniform, gathered at demonstrations in London outside parliament and in nearby Trafalgar Square, waving placards that said "save higher education" and "Fight for our futures not their wars."
"I've lost so much hope," Eliz, who had taken the day off from college and gave only one name, told AFP.
The 18-year-old said she was unsure whether she would go to university, "because of money. Because most jobs are getting taken over by AI. Everyone's just kind of more depressed."
There were scuffles between groups of right-wing and anti-fascist demonstrators, and AFP saw a handful of arrests.
Chants of "Palestine will live forever" rang out at the London protests, and Palestinian flags were on display at several of the demonstrations across Europe.
In Rome, high school students marched behind a banner that read: "We will take freedom if no one gives it to us – against the government, the war and the high cost of living."
There were scuffles in the Italian capital, with some protesters throwing bottles and smoke bombs at police.
- 'DREADFUL' SCHOOLS -
Demonstrators called for more funding for education and railed against increased military spending during protests in the Spanish capital Madrid.
Gabriela Gimeno Serrano, a 16-year-old high school student, said there were 33 students in her class with just one teacher.
"Classrooms are very small, the facilities are in an absolutely dreadful state," she told AFP, adding some schools were even plagued by rats and cockroaches.
Protests are set to extend into the weekend, with trade unions and housing associations calling for further demonstrations.
The protests come around the anniversary of the Yellow Vests movement in France, which rattled President Emmanuel Macron in 2018 and 2019. Demonstrations are planned there on Saturday.
The protests in European countries have in part been inspired by recent demonstrations in France, which have sometimes turned violent.
Those began when students demonstrated at high schools in mid-September to demand better learning conditions, fuelling a nationwide campaign against soaring prices, inadequate public services and police brutality.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UKM must uphold integrity in all decisions, says Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
BANGI: Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir has stressed that integrity must guide Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia's (UKM) administration, financial management and decision-making to sustain its excellence.
The UKM chancellor said transparency, accountability and checks and balances must go hand in hand with efficiency to strengthen public trust in the university.
"Transparency, accountability and checks and balances must move in tandem with efficiency, and it is through these practices that public trust in UKM can be strengthened," he said at UKM's 54th Convocation Ceremony today.
Also present were Tunku Ampuan Besar of Negri Sembilan Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud and Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz, who is also UKM pro-chancellor.
Tuanku Muhriz said that, following earlier turmoil, the university's board of directors and management had initiated various efforts to strengthen governance and improve administration quality.
These initiatives include establishing the Ad Hoc Governance Committee (AHGC) and appointing an independent consultant to assess UKM's governance practices, he said.
"The assessment was conducted over 32 weeks, covering UKM's governance, finance and procurement.
"This initiative reflects UKM's willingness to accept objective evaluation and implement reforms," he said.
He expressed appreciation to the board of directors and management for implementing the initiatives.
Tuanku Muhriz said strong governance depended not only on structures and procedures, but also on the values practised by the entire university community.
Referring to a report presented to him, he said governance standards could only be maintained if understood, practised and upheld by those leading, managing and serving the institution.
"Therefore, this new initiative is very timely. UKM's work culture must be anchored on trust, integrity, professionalism, good conduct and accountability.
"The development of the UKM Code of Conduct and the UKM Way guide is hoped to strengthen the appreciation of these values.
"Talent and leadership development is also carried out based on merit, competency and integrity, with every leader setting a good example in fulfilling their trust," he said.
Meanwhile, Tuanku Muhriz reminded graduates that receiving their degrees was not the end of their journey, but the beginning of greater responsibilities.
He hoped the knowledge and experience gained at the university would be used to contribute to society while upholding good manners, morality and the principles of truth.
"As alumni, uphold UKM's good name and maintain ties with the university. Contribute your knowledge, experience and expertise for the benefit of society and future generations," he said.
He also expressed appreciation for the establishment of the Tuanku Muhriz Royal Chair in Integrity and Good Governance as well as the Centre for Governance and Good Regulatory Practice.
Tuanku Muhriz also congratulated world-renowned track cyclist Datuk Mohd Azizulhasni Awang on receiving an Honorary Doctor of Philosophy in Sports Development.
He said the award recognised Azizulhasni's contributions to the development of sports in the country.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police seek help identifying man found dead in Mount Austin drain
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Police are seeking help from the public to identify a man found dead floating in a drain near a school in Taman Mount Austin here on Wednesday.
Johor Baru (South) police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffei said the man's identity remained unknown as no identification documents were found on him and his face was badly disfigured.
He said police received information about the discovery from a member of the public at 1.15pm.
"Preliminary investigations found no signs of foul play.
"Those with missing family members are urged to contact the Setia Indah police station chief at 07-351 6422," he said in a statement.
The body was sent to Sultan Ismail Hospital's forensic department for a post-mortem to determine the cause of death.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police probe fatal Jalan Jelatek crash involving Libyan driver
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 43-year-old motorcyclist was killed after his motorcycle was hit by a car driven by a Libyan man suspected of running a red light at the Jalan Jelatek intersection early today.
The victim died at the scene from severe injuries around 1am.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department deputy chief Superintendent Suffian Abdullah said the accident involved the victim's motorcycle and a car driven by a 32-year-old Libyan man.
He said preliminary investigations found that the victim was travelling from Taman Keramat towards Setiawangsa when the traffic light in his direction turned green.
"Upon reaching the intersection, a car travelling from Wangsa Maju, driven by the Libyan, is believed to have run a red light and hit the victim's motorcycle.
"The motorcyclist suffered severe injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene," he said in a statement today.
Suffian said alcohol and urine screening tests on the car driver returned negative results.
The driver has been arrested to assist investigations, with a remand application to be made today.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving.
If convicted, the driver faces imprisonment of between five and 10 years and a fine of RM20,000 to RM50,000.
Those with information can contact the Tun H S Lee Traffic police station at 03-2071 9999 or any nearby police station.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lorry driver fined RM5,000 for obstructing immigration officer at BSI
Article:
PONTIAN: A lorry driver was fined RM5,000 after
pleading guilty to obstructing an immigration officer
at the Sultan Iskandar Building (BSI) in Johor Baru last month.
The 29-year-old was fined by the Sessions Court, which convened at the Pekan Nanas Immigration Depot.
The incident occurred around oon on Oct 27 when the man, who was at an immigration inspection counter in the export zone, was barred from leaving Malaysia after being flagged over an income tax violation.
Dissatisfied with the explanation, he became aggressive, hurled abusive remarks and assaulted the officer.
He was arrested, while the lorry he was driving was seized for investigation.
The man was charged under Section 56(1)(g) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 for obstructing an immigration officer in the discharge of official duties.
Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency enforcement unit officer at BSI, Nur Syahida Amira Mohd Yazid, prosecuted.
The offence carries a maximum fine of RM10,000, imprisonment of up to five years, or both, upon conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NGO director remanded over RM85,468 fund misappropriation
Article:
KANGAR: A director of a non-governmental organisation has been remanded for four days to assist investigations into the misappropriation of RM85,468 of the organisation's funds.
Kangar magistrate's court assistant registrar Rashidah Azmi issued the remand order, which runs until Tuesday, to facilitate investigations into criminal breach of trust under Section 409 of the Penal Code.
The 31-year-old suspect arrived at the court at 8.50am today, escorted by police, and left at 9.18am.
He was arrested at the domestic arrivals hall of Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 2 (KLIA2) at 11.05am yesterday by officers from the Perlis police Commercial Crime Investigation Department.
Perlis police chief Deputy Commissioner Hamzah Hashim said the arrest followed intelligence gathering after the suspect arrived from Sabah, en route to Kuala Lumpur.
He said investigations into the criminal breach of trust case began on Nov 13.
Preliminary investigations found that the funds, belonging to an organisation based in Jalan Behor here, were transferred to the suspect's personal bank account through 32 transactions between March 2 and July 20.
If convicted, he faces a jail term of between two and 20 years, whipping and a fine.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Masked men caught on video stealing cables near TREC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A group of masked men were caught on video cutting and removing roadside cables in broad daylight near TREC Kuala Lumpur.
The 38-second video, shared on Threads, showed several men dressed in dark clothing and wearing face coverings
cutting and pulling cables
along a road near an overhead bridge.
They were then seen loading the cables before fleeing in two black vehicles — a pickup truck and a sedan.
Several people attempted to stop the vehicles by throwing traffic cones at them as they drove off, but failed.
The Threads user who shared the video claimed the incident happened near TREC, adding that the alleged theft took place openly in front of members of the public.
The user also claimed a security guard at the scene merely watched as the incident unfolded.
However, the exact location and time of the incident, as well as the identities of those involved, have yet to be verified.
The New Straits Times has contacted the police for confirmation and further details.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Houthis strike Riyadh after Saudi-led coalition's 'special operation' in Yemen
Article:
RIYADH: Yemen's Houthis launched strikes on the Saudi capital Riyadh on Saturday, after vowing reprisals for a "special operation" by the Saudi-led coalition fighting them.
Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in neighbouring Yemen's civil war this summer, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.
An AFP journalist reported hearing two explosions shortly after authorities issued an alert, later lifted, saying the city was "under a hostile aerial threat."
The coalition later said it had "intercepted and destroyed" three Houthi ballistic missiles headed for the capital.
The Iran-backed Houthis said on X that they were striking targets across Saudi Arabia, including in Riyadh.
The strikes came after the Houthis vowed revenge for the coalition's attack on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida and other targets on Friday.
The "special operation" hit smuggling and weapons-transporting operations in Hodeida, the coalition said.
It also involved attacks on Sanaa, Saada and Taiz governorates, marking an uptick in violence after months of hostilities.
The Houthis had vowed to hit the Saudi city of Jeddah and other Red Sea ports if Hodeida was attacked, while warning airlines that Saudi airspace was "unsafe." The group also threatened Riyadh's financial district and a power station in Al-Shuqaiq.
- 'SPECIAL OPERATION' -
Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said its forces had "targeted operational capabilities at Hodeida port that were used in smuggling operations and the transport of weapons and ballistic missiles."
The coalition also hit "military targets" in Sanaa, including  missile and drone facilities and a supply depot, he said on X.
The Houthis said coalition strikes had killed 41 people in the previous 24 hours. Yemen's Saudi-backed armed forces said dozens of airstrikes and drone attacks, as well as hundreds of artillery attacks, killed or wounded 193 Houthi fighters.
These figures were impossible to verify independently.
Two ballistic missiles were intercepted over the Jizan region near the Yemen border, the coalition spokesman said, with debris falling in Al-Shuqaiq.
The Houthi military spokesman said the group had targeted Al-Shuqaiq power station and Jizan port with "accurate and direct" strikes that caused "extensive damage."
Images of a damaged power station in Mocha after a coalition air raid were broadcast by the Houthis' Al-Masirah television.
The coalition strikes came after a Houthi attack struck a tower in Riyadh's financial district, the latest high-profile blow against the world's top oil exporter.
Witnesses told AFP that Riyadh's tallest skyscraper, housing Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, was damaged.
- 'AIRSPACE IS UNSAFE' -
After the coalition warned civilians to evacuate Hodeida port, the Houthis responded by threatening to hit Jeddah and other ports on the Saudi Red Sea coast.
The Houthis' Humanitarian Operations Coordination Centre sent emails to shipping companies and other bodies using Jeddah port, warning them to evacuate.
The group warned "all airlines that Saudi airspace is unsafe, as it will be the theatre of our operations in the coming hours, except for the holy airspace over Makkah and Madinah."
They also told people to avoid Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District, whose offices were evacuated weeks ago, calling it a "military target."
The two sides have exchanged attacks since a four-year truce in Yemen's civil war collapsed in July.
Early on Friday, the Houthis accused the Saudis of striking a civilian boat, killing 19 people.
Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces withdrew from areas near the Red Sea's Bab al-Mandab strait this month, ceding territory to the Houthis, who launched a sweeping offensive in September.
The group has now advanced close to Aden, the interim capital of the internationally recognised government which fled the Houthis' takeover of Sanaa in 2014.
The coalition intervened against the Houthis in early 2015, in a conflict that left hundreds of thousands dead and created one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.
The United Nations expressed concern on Friday over the ongoing attacks.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 6.7 magnitude earthquake hits central Peru
Article:
LIMA: A 6.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Peru on Friday, the Peruvian Geophysical Institute reported, with a preliminary report indicating no fatalities or serious damage from the tremor.
The earthquake occurred at 7.09pm (0009 GMT Saturday), 30km northwest of the city of Junin, at a depth of 129km.
Peru's National Emergency Operation Center (COEN) reported the quake was felt with moderate to strong intensity and that "monitoring continues in vulnerable areas."
The earthquake was also felt in the capital Lima, as well as Huanuco and Callao.
Peru is situated on the so-called Pacific Ring of Fire – an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin.
Seismologists say Peru experiences at least 400 earthquakes per year, three-quarters of which are so weak people do not feel them.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rat sightings raise food hygiene concerns at Pudu Market [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Fresh concerns over food hygiene have emerged after several rats were spotted crawling over and eating bean sprouts at a shop in Pudu Market.
The latest
incident went viral
after a TikTok livestream recording was shared by a user on Threads, prompting concerns over the cleanliness of the premises and the safety of food sold to customers.
In the footage, several rats can be seen on top of containers filled with bean sprouts.
The user who shared the recording  asked if  the bean sprouts exposed to the pests would be discarded or continue to be sold to customers.
The post drew numerous reactions, with netizens expressing disgust and questioning whether authorities had taken action against the shop owners.
A user, Shadanish, claimed the shop was still operating despite several previous issues.
Another user, Mimieymia8, questioned the authorities' response and urged the public to remain vigilant about food hygiene.
Meanwhile, a user identified as Adawiyah called on the Health Ministry to conduct an inspection and look into the allegations.
Previously, an activist from Persatuan Kebajikan Surplus, known as Abe, exposed the unhygienic conditions at a raw chicken processing outlet believed to be located at Pudu Market.
In the TikTok livestream, a rat was seen eating raw chicken in a large water-filled container.
The footage raised concerns over possible contamination.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thai police foil attempt to smuggle 750kg of syabu into Malaysia
Article:
KOTA BARU: Thai police foiled an attempt to smuggle 750kg of syabu worth 300 million baht (RM36.3 million) into Malaysia after seizing the drugs from a lorry in Nakhon Si Thammarat province on Wednesday.
The seizure was made by Thai Police after officers intercepted the lorry at 1.45am (Thai time), a Thai security spokesman said.
Two men, aged 31 and 40.
The spokesman said authorities had earlier received intelligence that a lorry would be used to transport drugs from northern Thailand to the southern region.
Investigations by Border Patrol Police Division 44 found that the lorry had travelled from Songkhla to Chiang Saen district in Chiang Rai on Nov 9 to collect the drugs before heading south again on Nov 18.
"A team set up a roadblock and intercepted the lorry around 1.45am.
"The lorry's floor had been modified into a double-layered structure, with a concealed compartment used to hide the drugs.
"About 750kg of syabu was found under the floor panels," he said.
The drugs were packed in wrappers carrying the branding of a popular Chinese tea sold widely in Malaysia.
The spokesman said both suspects admitted to transporting the drugs from Chiang Rai to Hat Yai, where they were to be smuggled into Malaysia.
The syndicate is believed to have used Hat Yai in Songkhla as a transit hub, with Malaysia as the final destination.
Investigations also found that the suspects were members of a transnational drug syndicate trafficking syabu from coastal areas in Chiang Saen, Chiang Rai, to southern Thailand.
Both men admitted to making several previous deliveries, earning one million baht (RM121,000) for each trip, he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DAP MP Khoo apologises over remarks on Kuala Terengganu Friday closure directive
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: DAP's Kota Melaka member of parliament Khoo Poay Tiong has publicly apologised for his remarks over the Kuala Terengganu City Council's (MBKT) directive requiring all business premises to close for two hours every Friday.
In a Facebook post today, Khoo acknowledged that his choice of words and tone in an earlier statement had caused misunderstanding, hurt the feelings and caused unease among the public, particularly Muslims.
He said he had no intention of questioning or belittling Islam, Friday prayers or Muslims' right to fulfil their religious obligations.
"I acknowledge that there were shortcomings in the way I conveyed my views. My choice of words and the tone of the post had caused misunderstanding, offended people and created unease among the public, particularly Muslims," he said.
Khoo said he respected Islam and Friday prayers, adding that as an elected representative and leader, he should have been more careful and sensitive when commenting on religious issues.
He also accepted the criticism and feedback, taking full responsibility for his earlier statement.
"Once again, I sincerely apologise to everyone who was offended or hurt by my earlier post. I will learn from this incident and be more careful," he said.
Yesterday, Melaka DAP chairman Khoo clarified that his earlier remarks were not intended to touch on religious sensitivities or belittle anyone's religious practices.
He said he was questioning the policy and its enforcement, which he claimed would also affect non-Muslim business operators.
Khoo's concern was the blanket enforcement of the directive through an official MBKT letter requiring all business premises, including non-Muslim-owned businesses, to close from 12.30pm to 2.30pm every Friday.
He also highlighted the penalties for non-compliance, including a RM2,000 fine, imprisonment or cancellation of business licences.
His remarks drew criticism from several political leaders, including Bentong MP Young Syefura Othman, also from DAP.
In a Threads post yesterday, Young Syefura said Khoo should not interfere in matters concerning Malays and Islam or attempt to dictate the administration of another state.
She warned that such interventions could alienate people and urged him to focus on his own responsibilities.
Meanwhile, Melaka PKR state leadership council acting chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim also called on Khoo to withdraw his statement and apologise over the issue.
In a Facebook post yesterday, Adam Adli said he disagreed with Khoo's remarks and advised him to respect the state's laws and religious sensitivities in the country.
He said Khoo should be mindful of the legal framework governing the matter and the sensitivities surrounding religious practices.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man convicted of sparking deadly LA fire as defence blamed fireworks
Article:
LOS ANGELES: A US jury on Friday convicted a man of setting a New Year's Eve fire that grew into one of several deadly 2025 blazes in Los Angeles, killing 12 people in the Pacific Palisades.
It was the second federal trial of Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, after the initial prosecution attempt left the jury deadlocked and ended in a mistrial.
The former Uber driver is scheduled for sentencing on March 17. He faces up to 40 years in prison.
Earlier this year, a separate jury leaned 10-2 towards acquitting Rinderknecht, but verdicts must be reached unanimously.
Jurors in the second trial were ordered not to take the previous proceedings or any mention of them into account in reaching their decision.
Friday's verdict was on two charges: destruction of property by means of fire and arson affecting property used in interstate commerce.
Rinderknecht had pleaded not guilty to both.
But after two days of deliberation, jurors found he used a lighter to ignite a brush fire near the wealthy Pacific Palisades neighbourhood.
Firefighters had thought they extinguished it, but later found that smoldering embers underground were carried by strong winds and erupted, tearing through the affluent area and ravaging thousands of homes.
It proved among the most destructive wildfires in California history.
Rinderknecht's defence attorney, Steven Haney, had argued there was no direct evidence that his client started the fire, and suggested errant New Year's Eve fireworks could be to blame.
But the prosecution said evidence including cell phone data put him at the scene.
Fierce winds fuelled the 2025 Los Angeles fires that resulted in a total of 31 deaths.
Alongside the blaze that devastated the Pacific Palisades, a second fire scorched Altadena, in northest Los Angeles, razing parts of the neighbourhood.
That fire was tied to an idle transmission tower owned by local power company Southern California Edison, whose sparks ignited dry vegetation.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTviral: My Chemical Romance concert reunites best friends after 15 years [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A My Chemical Romance (MCR) concert became an unexpected reunion for two former school best friends who had not seen each other in 15 years.
Sofiah Idrus, 36, was stunned when she spotted her long-lost friend, Ziana, among the crowd waiting to enter the National Stadium in Bukit Jalil yesterday.
The pair had last met while studying at St George's Girls' School in Penang.
Sofiah said she had been frantically searching for her make-up artist when she unexpectedly spotted Diana.
"I was rushing around trying to find my make-up artist when I suddenly spotted Ziana in the crowd.
"It happened completely by chance. That's why you can see me jumping up and down with excitement in the video," she said.
View on Threads
The reunion was all the more special as both women had been devoted MCR fans since their school days.
For Sofiah, reconnecting with an old friend at a concert by the band they grew up listening to made the moment even more memorable.
She later shared a video of their reunion on Threads, drawing heartwarming reactions from social media users.

Title: Selangor development must prioritise forest conservation, experts say
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Selangor must adopt more sustainable and integrated development planning, with greater emphasis on forest conservation and natural water retention areas, rather than relying mainly on widening drains and rivers to address flooding.
Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) senior lecturer in water resources and environmental systems Dr Azinoor Azida Abu Bakar said forest clearing for development must be scrutinised more thoroughly, even in areas that had been officially degazetted for development.
She said this was crucial to ensure rapid development and population growth in the state did not place further pressure on existing drainage systems.
"Good development planning must go beyond modernisation and economic value. It must also create cities capable of managing water sustainably, protecting residents and remaining resilient to climate change.
"This includes preserving catchment areas, protecting river buffer zones, increasing retention ponds, expanding green spaces in developing areas and adopting the environmentally friendly drainage concept introduced by the Drainage and Irrigation Department (DID).
"Forest clearing for development must be examined in greater detail. Even if an area has been degazetted for development, hydrological and environmental impact assessments should not be overlooked.
"Forests and natural land serve as water absorption and rainwater storage areas while regulating surface runoff. Losing these green areas increases surface runoff, contributing to flooding," she told Berita Harian.
It was previously reported that rapid development, including slope stabilisation works, can be seen in several areas around Bukit Cherakah, Jeram, Ijok, Puncak Alam and Bukit Kapar.
A BH drone survey also showed extensive clearing of land on the outskirts of Shah Alam to make way for development, raising concerns that it could contribute to increasingly frequent floods in surrounding areas.
Azinoor Azida said the loss of green spaces would change land use patterns and reduce the landscape's ability to absorb rainwater.
She warned that inadequate hydrological planning could worsen flooding in the affected areas and their surroundings.
"The impact of development must be assessed cumulatively, rather than looking at individual projects in isolation, as changes in upstream areas can increase water flow into downstream areas such as Shah Alam," she said.
Meanwhile, Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia (UTHM) Environmental Management lecturer Associate Professor Dr Haryati Shafii said excessive disturbance of forest areas for development must be taken seriously as it could trigger a chain of consequences for the environment, people and wildlife habitats.
"Where forests have been gazetted as Environmentally Sensitive Areas, the relevant laws must be observed. Development should not be allowed in such areas.
"While efforts by government agencies to improve infrastructure maintenance and drainage systems are important in addressing floods, these measures are insufficient if treated as the country's main flood management strategy.
"We must look at flooding more comprehensively. Floods are not caused solely by clogged drains, shallow rivers or inadequate drainage systems. They are also influenced by climate, hydrology, land use, physical development, ecology and human behaviour," she said.
Pertubuhan Pelindung Khazanah Alam Malaysia (Peka) called for a temporary suspension of existing development approvals and new projects involving forest reserves and hilly areas on the outskirts of Selangor.
It said an independent investigation should be conducted immediately to establish whether forest clearing activities had contributed to major and recurring floods in several parts of the state.
"Peka is calling for a development moratorium in affected areas, an audit of all previous approvals and an independent investigation into forest clearing activities and land degazettement," it said in a statement yesterday.

Title: US judge approves Bayer's US$7.25bil Roundup cancer settlement
Article:
WASHINGTON: A US judge on Friday approved Bayer's US$7.25 billion settlement of lawsuits over claims its Roundup weedkiller caused blood cancer, in one of the largest class-action payouts in US history.
The decision paves the way for compensation to tens of thousands of people who were exposed to the glyphosate-based herbicide and have been diagnosed with Non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL).
It also covers people who were exposed to Roundup and go on to develop the illness in the future.
The Missouri state court "fully and finally approves the Settlement Agreement in its entirety," Judge Timothy Boyer said in his ruling.
"Today is a real good day," Christopher Seeger, a court-appointed lead attorney for plaintiffs already diagnosed with NHL, told AFP by phone.
People with diagnosed NHL will receive payments of between US$10,000 to US$165,000, depending on a range of factors including whether they were residential or occupational users of Roundup, such as landscapers.
Approval of the settlement was "really the only path that most victims of Roundup will have to compensation," Seeger said, because in June, the US Supreme Court sided with Bayer in a case and ruled it would no longer allow "failure-to-warn" claims in US states.
The Supreme Court concluded that the US Environmental Protection Agency's determination that Roundup is not a carcinogen pre-empts claims in state courts tying the product to a cancer diagnosis.
Seeger explained that those claims had been the most viable path for most plaintiffs. This settlement was reached before the Supreme Court ruling, but both sides had agreed to honour it whatever the outcome.
People who never filed a case but were exposed to Roundup can still apply for compensation if they develop NHL in the coming years and if they meet certain conditions.
Bayer has spent billions of dollars settling thousands of cases linked to Roundup since it acquired the weedkiller's producer, the US agrichemical group Monsanto, in 2018. In a statement to AFP, it said it hoped the settlement, together with the Supreme Court decision, would help draw a line under litigation.
"The Court's final approval is a decisive milestone in the company's strategy to mitigate the risks of both pending and future Roundup litigation," said CEO Bill Anderson.
- 'PROBABLE CARCINOGEN' -
The World Health Organization's International Agency for Research on Cancer in 2015 designated glyphosate, Roundup's main active ingredient, a probable human carcinogen, but Bayer says scientific studies and regulatory approvals show the weedkiller is safe.
Last year, a highly influential decades-old study that declared Roundup posed no serious health risks was retracted, ending a decades-long saga that exposed how corporate interests can distort scientific research and influence government decision-making.
In its retraction note, the Regulatory Toxicology and Pharmacology journal cited a litany of serious flaws, ranging from the omission of carcinogenicity studies available at the time to undisclosed contributions by Monsanto employees.
Glyphosate was brought to market as a herbicide in the 1970s and initially welcomed as less toxic than DDT.
But its soaring use – especially after Monsanto introduced glyphosate-tolerant seeds that allowed it to be sprayed widely over crops – drew increasing scrutiny in the 1990s.
Several countries have since moved to restrict or ban its use, including France, which has prohibited household applications. Bayer said it was phasing out Roundup for US residential use in 2023 in response to growing lawsuits.--AFP

Title: Two children killed in fire at converted office building in Sik
Article:
SIK: Two children, a 16-month-old girl and a 3-year-old boy, were killed in a fire at an office building that had been converted into a house in Kampung Teloi Tua today.
Their bodies were found on a bed after the fire destroyed nearly 90 per cent of the building.
Kedah Fire and Rescue Department officer Fire Superintendent Bryan Del Bungkias said the department received an emergency call at 6.11am.
He said 10 firefighters from the Sik Fire and Rescue station were deployed to the scene.
Del Bungkias said the fire was brought under control at 6.50am.
Firefighting operations have been completed, while mopping up work is underway," he said.

Title: Negri political crisis: 24 BN, PN assemblymen agree to abide by party decisions
Article:
SEREMBAN: Twenty-four of the 25 Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional assemblymen in Negri Sembilan have agreed to abide by top leadership directives and party decisions to resolve the state's ongoing political crisis.
State BN chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the consensus was reached during a
special meeting
at Wisma Umno Negri Sembilan last night.
Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) assemblymen in Negri Sembilan have agreed to follow their party leaderships' decisions amid the ongoing political crisis in the state.
"At this special meeting, all the assemblymen, including PN assemblymen, reached a consensus to abide by and comply with any directive from the top leadership and party decisions.
"This is to ensure that the political crisis currently facing the state can be resolved promptly for the stability and prosperity of the people," he said in a statement.
Mohamad, who is also BN deputy chairman, chaired the meeting, which began at 9pm and lasted more than two hours.
Three assemblymen were absent, including Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, while two others were overseas.
The two assemblymen currently abroad — Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa (Serting) and Datuk Razali Abu Samah (Sikamat) — also expressed their full support for any decision made last night.
Separately, seven assemblymen
tipped for appointment
to the state executive council (exco) are understood to have signed letters of undertaking before Ismail at his office yesterday.
Those tipped for the posts include four Umno assemblymen: S. Leza Md Yasin (Pilah), Mohamad Qayyum Abd Jalil (Senaling), Datuk Mohd Zaidy Abdul Kadir (Jeram Padang) and Muhammad Sufian Maradzi (Seri Menanti).
Also named are MCA's Koh Kim Swee (Repah) and Wawasan's Ridzuan Ahmad (Gemas).
The swearing-in ceremony is understood to be scheduled for Sunday at Istana Seri Menanti in Kuala Pilah.
The developments come amid uncertainty over Ismail's position as menteri besar.
The controversy over Ismail's position arose on Monday night (Nov 16), when BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir announced on BN's official Facebook page that the Menteri Besar had resigned.
Zambry said BN chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had received a copy of the resignation letter purportedly addressed and sent to Tuanku Muhriz.
Ismail said yesterday that he would remain in office after Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir consented to retain him following an audience at Istana Hinggap.
He also said he had neither submitted nor agreed to the submission of the resignation letter.
However, the palace said Ismail must demonstrate that he still commands the support of a majority of state assemblymen to remain as menteri besar.
Negri Sembilan Royal Comptroller Datuk Azizi Mohamad Ali said Ismail must also submit a proposed list of state executive councillors for the ruler's consideration.
Azizi said the palace would comply fully with constitutional provisions and conventions in resolving the matter.
The Yang di-Pertuan Besar hoped the issue could be resolved promptly in the interests of the people of Negri Sembilan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump vows to veto Democratic bills but leaves door open to cooperation
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump pledged on Friday to veto legislation passed by Democrats when they take control of Congress in 2027, but said his veto power should be seen as a starting point for lawmakers who want to achieve change.
Speaking at a White House news conference, Trump called the presidential veto "extreme powers," and said his threat to block legislation would cause Democrats to moderate their policies.
"They're going to send things my way, and I'm going to veto them. And then they're going to send more things, and I'm going to veto them," Trump said. "And they could go two years and one month, because that's what we have, and I'm going to veto them."
Trump said Democrats may realise that to avoid his veto, they could work with him to accomplish legislative goals.
"Because of the power of the veto, there's a real possibility that we get a lot of great things done," he said.
Trump said many Democrats had called him to discuss healthcare and immigration reform and pointed to healthcare as an area where lawmakers from different perspectives might meet somewhere in the middle.
"I'm open to great healthcare now, especially on healthcare. I'm open to great healthcare now," he said.
"Can it be what they want? No, but it can be a combination of what we all want, and we could end up with great healthcare in our country."
With the new Congress set to choose its leadership soon, Trump described Senator Chuck Schumer, who is vying to become senate majority leader, and Representative Hakeem Jeffries, who is on the path to becoming the next house speaker, both from New York, as "smart" and expressed willingness to work together.
"If they want to get things done, I want to get things done too," Trump said.
Trump also said Democratic Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa had called him two days ago about the border and he thought they could find a solution.
"She was really nice. It was a very productive call, and she wants to have a strong border. And we'll be able. I think we'll be able to work something out," he said.--REUTERS

Title: Pahang aims to collect RM1.5b revenue
Article:
KUANTAN: The Pahang government is targeting a record revenue collection of RM1.507 billion next year, its highest projection in history.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said operating expenditure is estimated at RM1.502 billion, resulting in a projected surplus of RM5 million.
He said RM454.4 million had been allocated as development expenditure to finance various projects and programmes, with public welfare  a priority.
[[nid:1582371]]
"Pahang has exceeded the RM1 billion mark in revenue collection for five consecutive years.
"Up to Nov 19, the state had collected RM1.203 billion, or 94.05 per cent of this year's RM1.279 billion revenue target," he said when tabling the 2027 state budget at Wisma Sri Pahang yesterday.
Wan Rosdy said the 2027 Pahang Budget, themed "Pahang 1st:  Caring Government, People First" (
Kerajaan Prihatin, Rakyat Diutamakan
), was formulated based on three key considerations: financial capacity, development needs and the people's interests.
He said the state government had allocated RM245.61 million under Bantuan Prihatin Pahang since 2022 to ease the financial burden of the people, before continuing the initiative under Inisiatif Makmur Pahang (IM Pahang).
[[nid:1582370]]
"Next year, the initiative will be rebranded as
Inisiatif Bantuan Negeri Pahang
, consolidating all assistance programmes, including IM Pahang and Apresiasi Pahang 1st (state policy and development framework), to benefit those in need," he said.
He said among the new initiatives for next year is the RM2 million Pahang 1st Rental Deposit Subsidy Programme, which will help eligible  household heads in the state to secure rental accommodation, including those living outside the state.
Wan Rosdy said RM1.1 million has also been allocated for the Pahang Gig State Assistance Initiative, which provides a one-off RM300 contribution to registered gig workers who actively contributed to the Social Security Organisation's  Lindung Kendiri scheme.
He said the state would also introduce the Pahang 1st Interest-Free Motorcycle Purchase Subsidy Programme, with an allocation of RM3 million to offer interest-free loans to public and private higher-learning institution  students aged between 18 and 21.
On enforcement, he said the Pahang Enforcement Unit had recorded 158 arrests linked to illegal mining, contributing to a 124.9 per cent increase in state mineral revenue, from RM33.08 million in 2021 to RM74.4 million this year.
He said the state government would recruit 50 officers to strengthen enforcement and achieve zero land encroachment, bringing the unit's total workforce to 220.

Title: Iran seeks diplomatic deal to end war, but Trump rejects terms
Article:
BAGHDAD: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Teheran still hoped diplomacy could end its war with the United States, while US President Donald Trump said Iran wanted a deal but one that was not acceptable to him.
Araqchi told the state-owned Iran newspaper that Teheran was seeking "an agreement that would ensure there was no further war" and wanted guarantees that Washington was serious about negotiations before proceeding further, adding that Iran had discussed with mediators the form and nature of confidence-building measures.
The remarks came as diplomatic efforts continued to try to end a conflict that has destabilised the Middle East, disrupted shipping, driven up global energy prices and drawn in countries across the region
The foreign minister said Iran's red lines included keeping enriched uranium in the country, though he added that he believed "a fair solution" could be reached.
"They want to make a deal, but they don't want to make a deal that's acceptable to me," Trump said at a press conference on Friday.
The United States and Israel attacked Iran on Feb 28, prompting Teheran to strike Israel and Gulf states hosting US military bases.
Qatari and Iranian officials met on Tuesday in talks aimed at "bridging perspectives and narrowing the gap between proposals presented on the ground," a spokesperson for Qatar's foreign ministry said.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump threatens 'tremendous tax' on US firms building data centres abroad
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump threatened on Friday to impose a "tremendous tax" on US companies that build their data centres overseas, signaling a new push to try and cut China off from advanced computing power.
"We're not going to allow companies to build data centres in other countries. If they do that, they can. But we're going to put a tremendous tax on them," Trump told a news conference in Washington.
"China will take all of them, and we're not allowing that to happen."
On Monday, Washington moved to close a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centres in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on US hardware not available for export to China.
The new export controls require data centres anywhere in the world to have a US license to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other territories under US embargoes.
The breakneck development of artificial intelligence (AI) technology depends heavily on the construction of large electricity-hungry data centres, which have sparked political backlash in communities across the United States.
The data centres have pushed electricity rates higher, emit air pollution and consume vast amounts of water.
Trump cautioned that any slowdown in data center construction in the United States would impact its lead in AI, which his administration refers to as Super Intelligence (SI).
"Whoever wins SI, wins. And you want to take advantage of the data centres. Make them pay you. Make them pay your community," he said.
"But take advantage. Don't shut them off."
He also alluded to other unspecified "penalties" the administration could put on companies that build data centres abroad.  --AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Give him a second chance': Trump backs Huang's return to Nvidia
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Friday called for chip giant Nvidia to reinstate disgraced former CEO Jensen Huang after he resigned over extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
"I would love to see him be back. You have one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world, and where is he going to go?" Trump told reporters.
"I think that I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance."
Huang resigned last week as chief of Nvidia, a company at the centre of the AI revolution, after revelations of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy who may have funneled restricted chips to that country.
Reports of at least two further affairs emerged after that initial report, with US intelligence said to be aware of the possibility of the alleged Chinese espionage.
Trump defended Huang as "a good man" who "made some bad decisions."
"I'd like to see Jensen make a big apology and go back because he created something with Blackwell," he said, referring to the most advanced chips designed by Nvidia.
The US president also appeared to directly contradict his own treasury secretary, saying he had spoken to China's President Xi Jinping about Huang during a summit earlier this week.
"I did discuss that with President Xi, and he said, 'Oh, brilliant, brilliant! He's a brilliant man,'" said Trump.
Earlier in the day, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Trump had not discussed Huang with Xi during the meeting in Shenzhen.
Trump advocated for Nvidia to take back Huang as their CEO "if they were smart."
Huang has offered to return to the company, a move the chip giant's board has rejected.
Board chair Harvey Jones said in an earnings call this week that "the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."
- 'MUST STAY AHEAD' -
Earlier, Bessent had spoken at length about the AI race with China in comments to US broadcaster CNBC.
Speaking about the Trump administration's support for the domestic AI sector, Bessent stressed that the United States "must stay ahead" of China in that realm.
"Our best protection against the foreign SI and exploits by foreign actors is for our labs to maintain their substantial lead, and in effect, they are our shield against SI," he said, using the government's preferred SI, or "super intelligence."
"There's no turning back on this. What we have to do is make sure that our labs maintain their leads through their continued innovation, through their access to the best chips, and through smart policy."
Bessent said Trump and Xi had agreed on certain guardrails on the use of AI in the military domain.
"President Trump and President Xi agreed that humans should always be involved in any military decisions that SI makes, and the SI should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions," he said.
On the threat of AI-enabled cyberattacks, Bessent again stressed that the best defence his country had was to allow its AI companies "to continue at the frontier and to provide us with the best defense against these other models."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST CRIME WATCH: Week of shootings, armed clashes and million-ringgit scams [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A suspected robber linked to 24 cases was killed in a shootout with police, a worker was gunned down following an argument at a diesel depot, and a teenage girl was accidentally shot while fishing and catching frogs in Sabah.
Meanwhile, five RMAF personnel were nabbed for operating a drug smuggling syndicate.
The cases were among the week's major crimes, as police investigated violent offences, armed clashes and high-value scams nationwide.
Here are the major crime stories reported between Nov 15 and 18.
SUSPECTED ROBBER LINKED TO 24 CASES SHOT DEAD IN HOTEL SHOOTOUT
Police raided a hotel room in Chow Kit at 2am on Wednesday after tracking down a suspect wanted for a series of robberies.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the suspect opened fire on the police team, prompting them to return fire.
The suspect was killed in the shootout.
Police seized a weapon and substances believed to be syabu from the room.
Preliminary investigations found that the suspect had nine previous criminal records and was wanted.
Fadil said the suspect allegedly posed as a taxi driver before robbing passengers, particularly women, senior citizens and those he perceived as vulnerable.
Police believe his death has resolved 24 robbery cases, but investigations are continuing to determine whether others were involved.
The case is being investigated under Sections 392 and 397 of the Penal Code.
NST report: [Police shoot dead man linked to 24 robberies in Kuala Lumpur]
WORKER SHOT DEAD FOLLOWING ARGUMENT AT BUKIT TENGAH DIESEL DEPOT
A 41-year-old worker was shot dead, believed to be by a colleague, at a diesel storage depot in Bukit Tengah, Bukit Mertajam, Penang, on Nov 15.
The shooting occurred at 4.30pm, with the victim believed to have been shot three times by a colleague in his 40s.
The incident was believed to have stemmed from an earlier argument between the two.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the suspect fled after the shooting.
Police have launched a manhunt.
The victim's body was sent to hospital for a post-mortem examination. The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
NST report: [Man shot dead at diesel depot in Penang]
HUNTER ARRESTED AFTER TEENAGE RELATIVE SHOT IN NECK IN RANAU
A 15-year-old girl was seriously injured after being shot while fishing and catching frogs along Sungai Keliu in Kampung Tinamom, Ranau, Sabah, on Nov 14.
She sustained multiple wounds from a weapon believed to be an illegal homemade shotgun known as a "bakakuk".
Ranau police arrested a 40-year-old farmer the following day. Police confirmed he was related to the victim.
Investigations found that the suspect had gone hunting alone with a bakakuk before making his way along Sungai Keliu.
He reportedly mistook a light for the eyes of a mousedeer and fired a shot. He later heard screams and discovered that he had shot the teenager.
The girl was taken to Paginatan Health Clinic before being transferred to Ranau District Hospital and then Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Kota Kinabalu.
Police are trying to locate the weapon, which the suspect reportedly discarded in the forest.
The case is being investigated under the Arms Act 1960.
NST report: [Teen mistaken for mouse deer shot with homemade gun]
11 ARRESTED OVER ARMED BRAWL AT SANDAKAN MARKET
Police arrested 11 men following a fight between two armed groups at Pasar Bandar Ramai-Ramai in Sandakan, Sabah, on Nov 16.
Footage of the brawl at the busy market went viral on social media.
Sandakan police received information about the incident at 7.36pm.
Initial investigations found that a misunderstanding between the groups had started at midnight before escalating into a fight captured on video.
Police are investigating the motive behind the incident.
The case is being investigated under Section 148 of the Penal Code for rioting while armed.
NST report: [11 men arrested after Sandakan market clash]
SCAMMED: TWO WOMEN LOSE RM1.18 MILLION TO FAKE COPS
Two women in Johor and Terengganu lost RM1.18 million to phone scammers posing as police officers.
In Batu Pahat, a secondary school teacher lost RM748,326.50 after being duped by a scammer claiming to be a Bukit Aman police officer.
She was initially contacted by someone claiming to be from a hospital in Rawang, Selangor, who said a third party had used her name to make an insurance claim.
The call was transferred to a 'police officer', who offered to help her lodge an online police report and requested her ATM card to enable Bank Negara Malaysia to investigate.
The victim followed the instructions, leaving her ATM card at a nasi lemak stall beside her house.
She later discovered transactions totalling RM673,326.50 to accounts belonging to unknown individuals. She had also deposited RM75,000 into three bank accounts.
In a separate case in Kuala Terengganu, a 63-year-old retiree lost RM436,036 to a scammer posing as a police officer.
The suspect claimed she was involved in money laundering activities and that Bank Negara Malaysia had blacklisted her account for investigation.
The woman was instructed to pawn her jewellery, deposit the money into a bank account and leave her bank card beside a rubbish bin at a supermarket in Kuala Nerus.
She complied and later discovered withdrawals totalling RM436,036.
Both cases are being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.
NST reports: [Teacher loses RM750,000 in phone scam]
NST reports: [Elderly woman loses RM436k in money laundering phone scam]
FIVE RMAF PERSONNEL HELD OVER DRUG SMUGGLING SYNDICATE
Police arrested five Royal Malaysian Air Force personnel and six civilians over their alleged involvement in a cross-border drug trafficking syndicate believed to have used military air transport facilities to smuggle drugs from Peninsular Malaysia to Sabah before distributing them to international markets, particularly the Philippines and Indonesia.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the arrests were made during several operations in the Klang Valley and Labuan, Sabah, on Nov 17.
The operations, conducted following intelligence cooperation between the department and the RMAF Provost Marshal Branch, led to the seizure of 96.64kg of suspected methamphetamine worth RM4.83 million, as well as 6.98kg of liquid chemical substances.
Hussein said preliminary investigations found that the syndicate had been active since July, with two of the civilian suspects believed to have acted as coordinators.
Police are also tracking another Malaysian believed to be the syndicate leader to uncover its entire network and identify other individuals involved.
All five RMAF personnel were remanded for seven days from Nov 18 to 24, while the six civilians were remanded for between two and five days.
NST report: Five RMAF officers among 11 held over drug syndicate exploiting military air facilities
SUSPECTED ROBBERY GANG LEADER KILLED IN IPOH SHOOTOUT
In Perak, a 39-year-old man believed to be the leader of a dangerous interstate robbery gang was shot dead early on Thursday morning in an exchange of fire with police along Jalan Persiaran Lembah Perpaduan in Tambun, Ipoh.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said the incident happened when a joint team from Bukit Aman and the Perak police contingent conducting crime prevention patrols intercepted a suspicious Perodua Alza.
The suspect allegedly attempted to flee before opening fire at the police team, prompting officers to return fire in self-defence.
Kumar said the deceased had at least 17 previous criminal records and was believed to head a robbery gang.
Police recovered a pistol, ammunition and suspected methamphetamine from the deceased. A search of the vehicle also uncovered three machetes, face masks and various tools believed to have been used in house break-ins.
Kumar said another suspect had been arrested in Tanjung Malim, while four others remained at large.

Title: 'He is a killer': Zelenskyy hits back after Trump calls Putin his 'friend'
Article:
WASHINGTON: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy branded Vladimir Putin a "killer" in an interview broadcast on Friday, after President Donald Trump described the Russian leader as his "friend."
"For us he's an enemy, and of course, for us, he is a killer. And I think mostly for the people in the world, he is a killer," Zelenskyy told CNN in response to a question about Trump's description of Putin.
Trump and Putin held a meeting in China on Wednesday – their first since August 2025 – in which Trump called Putin his "friend" while the Russian president responded in English: "Nice to meet you."
Trump on Friday praised his ties with Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping during a press conference at the White House.
"I have fantastic relationships with Putin. That's a very good thing. I have fantastic relationships with President Xi. That's a good thing, and our country is safe because of that," Trump said.
Asked if he believed Putin was a friend to America, Trump said "I can't speak to America" but added that their "very good relationship... gives us a lot of additional strength."
Putin's forces launched an all-out invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, sparking a devastating war that is estimated to have killed hundreds of thousands of people.
Washington was Kyiv's primary backer under president Joe Biden, but Trump has slashed military support for Ukraine since returning to office at the beginning of last year.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST COURT WATCH: Week of murder acquittal, axe attack charge, cheating and high-profile court cases [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two men in Ipoh, Perak, were acquitted of murder, an unemployed man who posed as a royal aide-de-camp was jailed for cheating, and a 16-year-old boy was charged with wielding an axe and hurting his teacher.
In Perak, a man and his relative walked out of the High Court as free men after spending five years in remand over the alleged murder of a mentally ill man. However, the victim's death case continues against a third accused, who was ordered to enter his defence.
In Kuching, a 16-year-old boy claimed trial to charges of possessing an axe and explosives without lawful purpose, and voluntarily causing hurt to his teacher at an international school. The case came almost a month after a video of the student attacking his teacher went viral.
In Kuala Lumpur, an unemployed man who claimed to be an aide to the Raja Muda of Selangor and his fiancée faced multiple cheating charges involving a doctor and RM155,000, allegedly through bogus sales of two houses and a luxury car.
Also in Kuala Lumpur, Parti Pejuang Tanah Air president Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir failed in his bid to obtain leave for a judicial review challenging the Inland Revenue Board's demand for RM5.02 million in tax arrears for the 2017 to 2019 assessment years.
Meanwhile, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man are set to face off in a defamation trial next year over allegedly defamatory remarks made during a political speech in Pahang.
Below are several court cases which made headlines this week.
TWO MEN ACQUITTED OF MURDER AFTER FIVE YEARS
On Tuesday, the Ipoh High Court acquitted two men of murdering a mentally ill man after finding that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against them, bringing an end to their five years in remand.
Ismail Rizwan Ramli, 39, and his relative, Mohd Fuzi Ab Manaf, 52, were acquitted at the end of the prosecution's case.
However, Ismail's father, Ramli Lot, 65, was ordered to enter his defence on the murder charge.
The trio were jointly charged with murdering Muhammad Noor Faqih Mohamed Ariffin, 29, between 9.50am and 11.06am on Nov 25 at a morning market near the Jalan Hospital flats.
The incident reportedly stemmed from a dispute over a portable speaker that Faqih had allegedly stolen.
Police investigations found that Faqih had met Ismail and Fuzi at the scene on the day of the incident, where an argument broke out and escalated into a fight.
Ramli joined the altercation and allegedly grabbed Faqih by the neck from behind, causing him to become motionless and unresponsive. He was pronounced dead at the scene.
STUDENT CHARGED IN AXE ATTACK
Almost a month after a video of a student attacking his teacher went viral, a 16-year-old international school student was charged with three offences at the Kuching Magistrates' Court on Monday.
The boy, who cannot be named as he is a minor, was accused of carrying a small black axe without lawful purpose, voluntarily causing hurt to his 42-year-old teacher with the weapon, and possessing explosives without lawful excuse.
No plea was recorded and the court ordered him to undergo a psychiatric assessment.
The first charge alleged that he carried a small black axe as an offensive weapon without lawful purpose, an offence under Section 7 of the Second Schedule to the Corrosive and Explosive Substances and Offensive Weapons Act 1958.
The second charge accused him of voluntarily causing hurt to his teacher using the axe, under Section 324 of the Penal Code.
The third charge involved possessing firecrackers and modified beverage containers containing explosives under circumstances that gave rise to reasonable suspicion that they were not intended for a lawful purpose.
The charge, framed under Section 8 of the Explosives Act 1957, carries a maximum jail term of seven years, a fine of up to RM10,000 or both, upon conviction.
The court fixed Dec 17 for mention.
FAKE AIDE TO SELANGOR RAJA MUDA JAILED FOR CHEATING
On Tuesday, an unemployed man who posed as an aide-de-camp to the Raja Muda of Selangor and cheated a doctor of RM155,000 through bogus sales of two houses and a luxury car was sentenced to two years in jail and four strokes of the rotan.
Al Zulfadly Alias, 40, was immediately jailed after pleading guilty to four joint charges of cheating the doctor, who had been treating his fiancée, Nurul Nur Syahirah Kamarudin, 27.
The doctor had been promised delivery of the luxury car, but it was repeatedly postponed. A purported house ownership signing at an event also never took place.
The couple's scheme unravelled after the doctor checked with the Selangor Palace and discovered that Al Zulfadly was neither a special officer nor a personal bodyguard to the Raja Muda, nor an aide-de-camp or member of the palace staff.
While Al Zulfadly admitted to the offences, Nurul Nur Syahirah pleaded not guilty to the charges. She is scheduled to return to court on Dec 16.
DEFAMATION SUIT BETWEEN ANWAR AND PAS LEADER SET FOR TRIAL
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's defamation suit against Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man over allegedly defamatory remarks made during a political speech in Pahang is set to go to trial next year.
High Court judicial commissioner Moh Kok Wai will preside over the trial scheduled for May 11 to 15 and May 28 next year.
Anwar's suit concerns the publication and republication of the allegedly defamatory statements in video recordings and on Tuan Ibrahim's social media platforms.
Among the reliefs sought by Anwar are general, aggravated and exemplary damages, as well as an injunction to restrain Tuan Ibrahim from making, publishing, republishing or disseminating the statements or any statements carrying a similar meaning.
Anwar is also seeking the removal of the allegedly defamatory posts and any other relief deemed fit by the court.
MUKHRIZ FAILS IN RM5M TAX ARREARS CHALLENGE
On Monday, Parti Pejuang Tanah Air president Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir failed in his bid to challenge the Inland Revenue Board's (IRB) demand for more than RM5 million in tax arrears for the 2017 to 2019 assessment years.
High Court judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad dismissed the former Kedah Menteri Besar's application for leave to commence a judicial review, ruling that the dispute should first be brought before the Special Commissioners of Income Tax through the appeal mechanism under the Income Tax Act 1967.
The court found no exceptional circumstances to justify bypassing the statutory appeal process and seeking judicial review.
Mukhriz was also ordered to pay RM5,000 in costs to the IRB.
TEACHER'S JAIL TERM INCREASED FROM FOUR TO 10 YEARS
An Arabic-language teacher will spend six more years in jail after the Court of Appeal increased his sentence from four to 10 years for sexually assaulting an eight-year-old female pupil seven years ago.
On Wednesday, the three-member bench, chaired by judge Datuk Mohamed Zaini Mazlan, unanimously dismissed Ahnaf Afiq Shairul Bazri's appeal against his conviction but allowed the prosecution's cross-appeal for a heavier sentence.
Zaini, sitting with Datuk Ahmad Shahrir Mohd Salleh and Datuk Dean Wayne Daly, increased the four-year jail term for an offence under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017 to eight years, while maintaining the additional two-year jail term imposed under Section 16(1) of the same Act. Both sentences are to run consecutively.
Zaini said the original sentence was inadequate, considering the victim's age and the teacher's position of trust.
He said the accused had abused the trust placed in him as a teacher responsible for pupils' care and education.
The court also ordered Ahnaf to undergo counselling and police supervision for two years after completing his 10-year jail term.
A committal warrant was issued for him to begin serving his sentence immediately.
FATHER DENIES NEGLECTING SON IN NILAI TOLL PLAZA INCIDENT
A 45-year-old engineer from China claimed trial at the Seremban Sessions Court to a charge of putting his 12-year-old son at risk of physical harm by allegedly abandoning him near the Nilai toll plaza.
Jiao Bo entered his not guilty plea after the charge was read out in Mandarin.
He allegedly committed the offence at the toll plaza exit at 1.21pm on Nov 9.
The incident was said to have stemmed from a quarrel between Jiao's two children while they were travelling in a car.
He allegedly left one of the children behind as punishment.
Jiao faces a maximum fine of RM50,000, imprisonment for up to 20 years, or both, if convicted under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001.
The court set bail at RM20,000 with two Malaysian sureties and ordered Jiao to surrender his passport and not interfere with the child.
The court fixed Dec 17 for mention.
