Title: First ECRL ride? It’s your chance to explore some East Coast attractions and sample some great local eats
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — Beyond the platforms of the three main East Coast terminal stations is a variety of local food, cultural attractions and leisure activities awaiting travellers on board the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL).
This really is the perfect opportunity to explore what Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan have to offer.
KotaSAS
The first major stop is KotaSAS Station in Pahang, located approximately eight kilometres from Indera Mahkota, a suburb of Kuantan, and 10 kilometres from the city centre.
It serves as the main Express stop for the state capital, with the journey from Terminal Bersepadu Gombak taking approximately one hour and 35 minutes.
KotaSAS, also known as Kota Sultan Ahmad Shah, is Pahang’s new state administrative centre, comprising a planned township of government buildings, residential developments and commercial areas on the western outskirts of Kuantan.
For visitors, the station serves as a gateway to Kuantan which lies along the Kuantan River near the South China Sea.
Travellers can get around Kuantan using e-hailing services such as Grab or the Bas.my city bus network.
Restoran Satay Zul is among Kuantan’s best-known eateries offering grilled chicken, beef, rabbit and venison skewers every evening until around midnight.
Another local favourite is Restoran Akob Patin House, known for its ikan patin masak tempoyak (catfish cooked in fermented durian gravy).
Teluk Cempedak is a popular beach located approximately five kilometres east of Kuantan city centre and about 15 kilometres from KotaSAS Station.
Another attraction worth visiting is Kuantan 188, a 188-metre observation tower situated along the banks of the Kuantan River. It is the tallest tower on the East Coast of Peninsular Malaysia and the country’s second-tallest observation tower, after KL Tower.
Kuala Terengganu
The second major stop is Kuala Terengganu Station in Terengganu, approximately 8.7 kilometres from Bukit Payong, a suburb of Kuala Terengganu and 23 kilometres from the city centre.
It serves as the main Express stop for the state capital, with the journey taking approximately one hour and 25 minutes from KotaSAS, or two hours and 52 minutes from Terminal Bersepadu Gombak.
Kuala Terengganu sits at the mouth of the Terengganu River and is known for traditional boat-building, batik and songket.
With no feeder bus service yet, travellers can use e-hailing services such as Grab, take a taxi or rent a car to get around the city.
For a taste of classic Terengganu cuisine, head to Restoran Nasi Dagang Atas Tol, where the signature nasi dagang features rice steamed with coconut milk and served with fish curry.
Travellers can also sample nasi kerabu, another local favourite featuring blue-tinted rice served with a mixture of finely sliced herbs and vegetables, paired with various dishes at Suerasa Nasi Kerabu in the city.
Reflecting the city’s Islamic heritage, there are two mosques here, each with its own distinctive appeal, which are worth a visit.
One is the Crystal Mosque, or Masjid Kristal, which stands out for its sleek, modern design, incorporating steel, glass and crystal; the other is the Tengku Tengah Zaharah Mosque (Floating Mosque), the first floating mosque in Malaysia.
Kota Bharu
The third and final stop is Kota Bahru Station in Kelantan, approximately 9.2 kilometres from the city centre.
It serves as the main Express stop for the state capital, with the journey taking approximately one hour from Kuala Terengganu, or three hours and 52 minutes from Terminal Bersepadu Gombak.
Kota Bharu, which sits near the mouth of the Kelantan River, is known for its traditional crafts as well as its distinctive culinary offerings.
While a new terminal has yet to be built adjacent to the ECRL station, travellers can use Grab, take a taxi or rent a car to get around the city.
For a taste of the famed roti titab, travellers can head to Kopitiam Kita, where the dish originated. It features thick slices of bread toasted with butter, topped with kaya and a runny half-boiled egg.
Then there is nasi Kak Wok, a popular mixed rice dish said to have originated in Kota Bharu, at Nasi Kak Wok Lundang, located behind Kota Bharu Medical Centre along Jalan Dato Panglima Perang.
The eatery is among the local spots associated with the dish’s late founder, Mek Wook Hassan, fondly known as “Kak Wook”.
In the city, travellers can visit Pasar Besar Siti Khadijah, a vibrant market known for its predominantly female traders, while Istana Jahar and the surrounding heritage quarter offer a glimpse into the history of Kelantan’s royal court.

Title: From factory floor to AI, Micron Malaysia employees chart career paths through skills development
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 —  From starting as an operator to training others, and from working in component assembly to exploring artificial intelligence (AI), employees at Micron Malaysia are building their skills and advancing their careers as manufacturing processes become increasingly sophisticated.
Nor Shamim Mat Saffar, who joined Micron as an operator in 2019, has completed Levels 2 and 3 of the Malaysian Skills Certificate (SKM) and progressed to training others.
Her initial work in surface mount technology front-of-line operations provided a foundation in manufacturing, safety, quality and adherence to standard operating procedures.
“Don’t be afraid to start as an operator. I started as an operator myself, and that was where I built the foundation of my career. Keep learning, build your skills and don’t be afraid to take opportunities when they come your way,” she said in a statement.
Nor Shamim hopes to pursue a diploma and eventually take on a supervisory role, while the company’s shift arrangements help her balance work and family responsibilities.
Another employee, process engineer Kevin Lee Kar Heng, who joined Micron in January 2021 in the component assembly team, has been involved in Autonomous Defect Classification, which uses AI to support automated defect screening.
He has also used generative AI tools to accelerate his learning, including while developing a Power BI dashboard.
“For me, engineering is a bit like detective work. You see a problem, you look at the data, figure out what’s happening and try to solve it. That’s the part I enjoy. And now with AI, there are so many more things we can try and learn,” he said.
Lee’s professional development has extended to technical papers, research collaborations and conference participation, alongside leadership in initiatives under the Mosaic employee resource group.
He also values Micron’s management and technical career pathways, which enable technical contributors to progress while remaining close to the work they enjoy.
“Going forward, I want to keep challenging myself, take on bigger problems and continue growing, while staying close to the technical work that I enjoy.
“We should give ourselves the chance to explore. That’s how you discover what really fits you. Ultimately, passion and personal fit are often discovered by doing, not simply by thinking about them,” he said.
Micron Malaysia said its investment in employees encompasses AI upskilling, skills development and programmes supporting graduates and future leaders.
“As manufacturing becomes more sophisticated, team members have opportunities to build capabilities in areas including advanced manufacturing, automation, data analytics, AI-enabled processes, engineering, quality and reliability,” it said.
The company said its teams support leading-edge assembly and testing across solid-state drives, NAND flash memory, dynamic random-access memory for personal computers (PCDRAM) and memory modules, alongside product qualification and engineering.
This includes its world-first high-capacity 256GB low-power dynamic random-access memory (LPDRAM) SOCAMM2 module, produced in Penang for next-generation AI data centre infrastructure.
The company said the value of AI is about more than speed, as it also enables employees to learn, experiment and share knowledge so that more people can contribute to innovation.
Micron Malaysia said its investment in employees extends beyond skills and career development through its Total Rewards approach, which recognises contributions through competitive compensation and performance-based rewards.
Eligible employees also have opportunities to share in the company’s long-term growth.
The company said its wellbeing approach spans physical, mental, social, career and financial wellbeing to support employees across different aspects of their working lives.
In Malaysia, initiatives include health and wellness coverage, meal subsidies, confidential counselling and employee advocacy resources, alongside continued improvements to workplace facilities and experiences.
Micron established its operations in Muar, Johor, in 2010 before making a greenfield investment in Penang in 2018, developing its memory and storage manufacturing capabilities, engineering expertise and talent in Malaysia. — Bernama

Title: Accountant finds stress relief in origami, turns 1,111 paper folds into eye-catching 3D arch
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — Spending her days immersed in figures and financial statements has not stopped an accountant from expressing her creative side through the art of paper folding, or origami, with her three-dimensional (3D) craft creations attracting considerable attention.
For Wan Nur Saaraa Wan Manshol, the traditional Japanese art form, which she has been practising for more than 30 years, is more than just a hobby to fill her leisure time. It has also become a form of therapy to calm her mind and relieve stress after a hectic day at work.
What began as a way to relax has since evolved into something more remarkable, with the 45-year-old successfully creating a 3D origami arch using 1,111 origami units, showcasing how the art form can be transformed into unique and creative decorative pieces.
Known as the Kusudama Arch, the creation, made using the Kusudama Sonobe technique and comprising 38 paper balls of various sizes and 151 heart-shaped ornaments, attracted visitors’ attention during the World Origami Day celebration held here recently.
“Last year, I made a lampshade using paper, but this time I wanted to try something different by creating an arch. I wanted to show that origami can also be used as an attractive decorative element, especially in 3D form,” she told Bernama.
Met at the exhibition recently, Wan Nur Saaraa said that besides the creation, which took a week to complete, she had also showcased several other works, including Sonobe Light Haven, The Sonobe Lucky Cat, Songket in Fold and Batik in Love Fold.
Wan Nur Saaraa, who is affiliated with the Malaysia Origami Academy and has no intention of turning the art into a source of supplementary income, said origami had similarities with her profession as an accountant, as both required precision and balance.
“As an accountant, every account must balance. It is the same with origami. If the folds are not balanced, the final shape will not look beautiful. There is a different sense of satisfaction when I successfully complete a piece, and it helps relieve stress. It is the most affordable hobby.
“All you need is paper. Newspapers or paper bags can also be used, as long as you have patience and precision. I hope more people will give it a try because it can help sharpen creativity and calm the mind,” she said, adding that she hoped to create larger and more challenging origami pieces in the future.
Meanwhile, for Naqeeb Mateen Mohamad Najmuddin, 9, paper folding is an enjoyable activity that allows him to create various animal shapes, including snakes, Godzilla, fish, crabs and parrots.
“Because it looks cool,” said the Year 2C student at the Malaysia Origami Academy.
Elaborating further, his mother, Harizah Hanim Mohamed, said her eldest son’s interest began last year after he became fascinated by the various shapes that could be created through the craft, which he initially learnt by watching videos on YouTube.
This prompted her and her husband to enrol Naqeeb Mateen in origami classes early this year to nurture his interest and talent in paper folding, as the boy was less inclined towards sports activities.
“Since joining the academy, he has become more focused because origami is like mathematics, teaching children to understand each folding step carefully. Participating in exhibitions also helps build his courage and self-confidence,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Kedah records 406 fatal motorcycle accidents in 10 months, 72 involving under-18 riders
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Nov 20 — A total of 406 fatal accidents involving motorcycles were recorded in Kedah between January and October this year, with 72 of these cases involving riders under the age of 18.
Kedah police contingent headquarters (IPK) Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT) chief, Superintendent Abdel Nasser S. Salleh, said these statistics indicate that the safety of motorcyclists particularly teenagers requires serious attention.
He emphasised that the police take a stern view of unauthorised modification of motorcycles which deviates from established specifications as well as “street hooliganism” (reckless riding/illegal racing), as these actions not only endanger the riders themselves but also pose a threat to other road users.
“Seized motorcycles may be reclaimed, subject to compliance with stipulated terms and procedures including replacing non-compliant components with original parts or approved standard components,” he said in a statement here today.
He added that the police would ensure the release process for these motorcycles is carried out in accordance with prevailing legal provisions.
Abdel Nasser said enforcement efforts will continue to be intensified to ensure that road users adhere to established laws and regulations.
He also urged the public especially the youth and parents to play their part in ensuring that the motorcycles being used are kept in a safe condition and comply with the required specifications.
“Do not turn public roads into a racetrack. Make safety your top priority,” he said.
For the record, 3,282 motorcycles have been seized across Kedah during the same period, as part of ongoing enforcement operations conducted throughout the state.
Among the violations detected were modifications to motorcycle components that did not comply with established specifications including the exhaust, swingarm, rims, and other parts. — Bernama

Title: Man who posed as Selangor royal aide gets 27 more months’ jail, two strokes of cane for vehicle scam
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 20 — A man who impersonated an Aide-de-Camp (ADC) to the Raja Muda of Selangor and had been sentenced to imprisonment for fraud involving property and luxury vehicle purchases was sentenced to another 27 months’ imprisonment and two strokes of the cane today for similar offences.
Today, Al Zulfadly Alias, 40, was sentenced by the Magistrate’s Court here to a total of 27 months’ imprisonment and two strokes of the cane for cheating two victims of RM73,000 in a vehicle auction scam.
Magistrate Wan Noora Nisa Ngadirin meted out the jail sentence and fine after Al Zulfadly pleaded guilty to the charges.
The court ordered the prison terms to run consecutively, effective from the dates he was charged with the offences.
Meanwhile, Al Zulfadly’s fiancée, Nurul Nur Syahirah Kamarudin, 37, pleaded not guilty to the same charges. The court fixed Jan 19, 2027, for mention.
Today’s proceedings focused on the presentation of facts in Al Zulfadly’s case and the sentencing.
The couple was accused of conspiring with a 43-year-old man to deceive a 48-year-old man by falsely claiming they could facilitate the purchase of a used Honda CR-V, purportedly acquired through an auction held in conjunction with the ASEAN Summit, for RM33,000.
The offence was allegedly committed at a premises here between May 13 and 14.
The charge was framed under Section 109 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 420 of the same Code, which provides for a maximum jail term of 10 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Al Zulfadly was sentenced to 12 months’ imprisonment and one stroke of the cane for the offence.
The couple was also jointly charged with deceiving a 43-year-old woman by claiming they could facilitate the purchase of a used Lexus RX350, purportedly acquired through an auction held in conjunction with the ASEAN Summit, for RM40,000.
The offence, framed under Section 420 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34, was allegedly committed at a premises in Taman Sri Andalas here between April 13 and 14.
Al Zulfadly was sentenced to 15 months’ imprisonment and one stroke of the cane for the offence.
According to the case facts, the male victim met the couple at a restaurant to obtain information about the sale of used vehicles in conjunction with the ASEAN Summit.
During the meeting, Al Zulfadly introduced himself as an ADC to the Raja Muda of Selangor and claimed he could arrange the purchase of vehicles through an auction.
He allegedly used his purported position to convince both victims that he could secure vehicles for them at lower prices.
Believing his claims, the victims transferred RM33,000 and RM40,000, respectively, into a bank account belonging to Al Zulfadly. However, neither received the vehicles as promised.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Amirah Zahari urged the court to order the prison terms to run consecutively, citing the seriousness of the offences, particularly the impersonation of an ADC to the Raja Muda of Selangor.
“The accused deceived two complainants, who believed he possessed the influence to facilitate the purchase of vehicles. This severe sentence serves as a clear message to the public that the court views such offences with the utmost seriousness and will not compromise with those who break the law.
“It is also hoped that this sentence will serve as a lesson to both the accused and the public, as a deterrent against similar offences,” she said.
However, Al Zulfadly’s lawyer, Yong Kum Lam, from the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK), appealed for a lighter sentence, saying his client was unemployed and remorseful.
The couple was initially charged at the Shah Alam Magistrate’s Court on Nov 12 with cheating involving the sale of an auctioned vehicle worth RM33,000.
The following day, Nov 13, they were charged at the Klang Magistrate’s Court over the RM40,000 vehicle scam. The case was subsequently transferred to the Shah Alam court.
On Nov 16, Al Zulfadly was sentenced to one year’s imprisonment and two strokes of the cane by the Kuala Lumpur Magistrate’s Court after pleading guilty to cheating a celebrity in a property purchase scam.
The following day, he was sentenced by the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court to two years’ imprisonment and four strokes of the cane after being convicted on four counts of cheating a female doctor of RM155,000 involving property and luxury vehicle purchases. — Bernama

Title: Police seize RM1.27m in health, cosmetic and food products in Banting raid, three held
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 20 — Police detained three individuals and seized health, cosmetic and food products worth RM1.27 million during a raid at a logistics premises in Banting, Selangor yesterday.
The operation, codenamed Op Taring Dosej, was carried out at 12.10 pm by the Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Intelligence Investigation (WCB/PSK) under the Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA), together with several enforcement agencies.
Bukit Aman JKDNKA WCB/PSK commander SAC Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said those detained comprised a local man believed to be the company owner and two Bangladeshi men employed at the premises.
He said checks found 1,044 boxes of health and cosmetic products, 1,300 bottles of supplements and health products, 38 boxes of pure tremella soup products, 65 boxes of coenzyme Q10 products and various tea-based food and beverage items and snacks.
“All the seized items have been handed over to the respective enforcement agencies for further action and investigation under their respective jurisdictions,” he said in a statement today.
The total value of the seizure is estimated at RM1.27 million. The Ministry of Health (MOH) recorded the highest seizure value at RM1.26 million, followed by the Kuala Langat District Health Office at RM5,167 and the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) at RM4,745.
Also participating in the operation were the MOH Selangor State Pharmacy Division, KPDN, the Royal Malaysian Customs Department Klang Branch, the Kuala Langat District Health Office and the Kuala Langat Municipal Council (MPKL).
In the same operation, the Kuala Langat District Health Office issued two compounds totalling RM4,500. MPKL issued two compounds amounting to RM2,000.
The case is being investigated under the Immigration Act 1959/63, the Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984, the Trade Descriptions Act 2011, the Food Act 1983 and related regulations.
Mohd Zaki said police would continue to strengthen enforcement and intelligence operations to address smuggling and the distribution of illicit goods. — Bernama

Title: Lorry driver in Sabah to face trial in April 2027 over alleged sexual offence against stepdaughter, 16
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 20 — A 33-year-old lorry driver charged with committing physical sexual harassment against his stepdaughter, will go trial on April 7 and 8, 2027.
Sessions Court Judge Zaini Fishir set the date for the man whose case was brought up for pre-trial case management to serve all the relevant documents.
The man is accused of committing the offence by fondling the breasts of the 16-year and ten-month-old girl for the purpose of sexual at 5am August 22 this year at a house in Tuaran.
The offence under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, carries a jail term of up to 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
The court had released the man on bail of RM10,000 with RM5,000 deposited in two local sureties after granting his application of bail through his counsel.
The man also was ordered to report to Kundasang police station once a month pending the disposal of his case.
Earlier, counsel Jagnesh Jaya who defended the man, applied for bail to be granted as in previous proceedings in Tuaran Sessions Court, the man was not granted bail.
Jagnesh told the court that the man who has four children, has no counsel at that time he was charged in court and asked for a lower bail.
However, Deputy Public Prosecutor Fazriel Fardiansyah Abdul Kadir objected the application but if the court allow the application, Fazriel had suggested the bail sum of RM10,000.
Meanwhile, a 42-year-old man was fined RM100 or seven days’ jail for failing to explain how he had in possession the three packets of instant drinks believed to be stolen.
Azmi Mohd Ayub@ Md Ayub pleaded guilty before Magistrate Dzul Helmy Yunus, to failing to give reasonable explanation about the instant drinks at 11pm on November 12 this year at a supermarket in Lido, Penampang. — Daily Express

Title: ‘Qibla marker’ on Mount Kinabalu is a prayer aid, not a religious privilege, says Sabah mufti
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 20 — The provision of a qibla (direction of prayer) marker on Mount Kinabalu is a basic facility for Muslims to perform prayers and is not intended to grant exclusive rights to any religion, said Sabah Mufti Datuk Dr Bungsu @ Aziz Jaafar.
In a statement today, he explained that the presence of the marker indicating the direction of Kaabah did not mean that the rights of followers of other religions to practise their respective faiths on the mountain were being denied or sidelined.
“The presence of the qibla marker does not in any way prevent followers of other religions from praying or practising their respective faiths on the mountain.
“There is no such thing as exclusive privileges for any particular religion on Mount Kinabalu,” he said, adding that anyone could engage in religious activities, subject to their needs and approval from Sabah Parks.
Bungsu said the installation of a qibla marker was also not carried out arbitrarily, as it required official verification from an authorised body such as the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) or the relevant religious department to ensure its directional accuracy.
He said followers of other religions, including Christians, Hindus, Buddhists and those of other faiths, are welcomed to submit proposals for specific facilities to Sabah Parks management for consideration, subject to suitability and park regulations.
On the issue of fairness to followers of all religions, he explained that equal treatment should not be measured by providing identical facilities for all religious practices. Instead, it should ensure that every visitor is respected and given the space to practise their faith without infringing on the rights of others.
“The public should not confuse the provision of facilities for one religion with granting privileges that deny the rights of other religions, as the qibla marker is merely a directional guide and facility, not an obligation,” he said.
However, he stressed that safety and compliance with the standard operating procedures (SOP) for climbing activities remained the absolute priority and must not be compromised by any religious or cultural activities.
He also reminded the public that Mount Kinabalu remained open to all segments of society, and that the responsibility of safeguarding the safety and sustainability of the natural treasure must be shared by everyone.
Previously, the installation of a qibla direction marker on Mount Kinabalu went viral on social media, becoming a topic of discussion among netizens. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB disowns resignation letter submitted to Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 20 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has clarified that he never authorised the submission of his resignation letter to Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, contrary to reports on Monday.
He said the letter had been kept by the party leadership but stressed that he had never consented to its submission under such circumstances.
“I did not personally submit the resignation letter to His Royal Highness. The letter was indeed kept by the party leadership, but I never agreed to it being submitted in that manner.
“I only learnt about it through social media, and His Royal Highness also did not accept the way it was done. I neither submitted nor consented to the letter being presented to His Royal Highness. I do not even know who delivered it,” he told a press conference at the Menteri Besar’s official residence here today.
Earlier, Ismail was granted an audience with Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Hinggap, which was also attended by Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid, Undang Luak Sungai Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari and Undang Luak Jelebu Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi.
Following the audience, Ismail, who is also Juasseh assemblyman, said Tuanku Muhriz had decreed that he continue serving as Menteri Besar to ensure continuity in the state administration.
The controversy over Ismail’s position arose on Monday night when Barisan Nasional (BN) secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, in a statement posted on BN’s official Facebook page, announced that the Menteri Besar had resigned.
Zambry said BN chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had received a copy of the resignation letter purportedly addressed and sent to Tuanku Muhriz.
On Tuesday, the Negeri Sembilan Palace clarified that a Menteri Besar’s resignation would only take effect with the consent of Tuanku Muhriz, in accordance with the State Constitution.
Meanwhile, Ismail said the state government’s immediate priority was to restore the smooth functioning of its administration, which had been disrupted by the absence of State Executive Council (Exco) members.
He said the situation had prevented many government decisions from being made as the Exco meetings could not be held.
“The state administration has been significantly disrupted because there are no Exco members. Therefore, I will seek Tuanku Muhriz’s consent to appoint new Exco members as approved by His Royal Highness,” he said.
Ismail stressed that the appointments were subject to Tuanku Muhriz’s consent, adding that a list of proposed Exco members had yet to be prepared but would be finalised as soon as possible.
He said discussions on the dates of the State Legislative Assembly sittings, including the tabling of the state budget, would only take place after the Exco appointments were settled.
On adat issues linked to the state’s political turmoil, Ismail said such issues should be resolved through the appropriate adat procedures without disrupting the administration of the state government. — Bernama

Title: Four years’ jail, counselling and police supervision for Sabah pensioner , 69, convicted of child sex offence
Article: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 20 — A 69-year-old pensioner was sentenced to four years’ jail for committing sexual physical harassment against a minor.Sessions Court Judge Noor Hafizah Mohd Noor imposed the sentence to Jamran Abdul Majit after ruling that the prosecution had proven its case beyond reasonable doubt against Jamran.He was found guilty of committing the sexual abuse on the 10-year and eight-month-old girl by touching the victim’s breast, stomach and grabbed the victim’s private part at 3pm on July 18, 2024, inside a shop in Manggatal, here.Jamran was convicted under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, carries a jail term of up to 20 years and whipping upon conviction.Jamran was ordered to undergo rehabilitative counseling while serving the jail sentence and to be placed under police supervision for three years after completing the jail term.The court ordered Jamran to serve the jail sentence from the date of his conviction on Thursday.However, the court granted Jamran’s application to stay execution pending appeal against the decision to the High Court and released on the same bail and conditions as previous one.Six prosecution and two defence witnesses had testified in the hearing.During mitigation, counsels Mohamad Syazwan Shah together Nigel Neong Kaning who defended Jamran, asked for a minimum sentence saying that Jamran was a pensioner and has a wife who is depending on him.Syazwan told the court that Jamran was also suffering from several medical conditions such as thyroid, cholesterol, prostrate having problem, severe back pain and currently receiving treatment from the Queen Elizabeth Hospital 2 and Manggatal Health Clinic.He also added that it was Jamran’s first offence.However, Deputy Public Prosecutor Fazriel Fardiansyah Abdul Kadir who conducted the prosecution, urged the court to impose a heavy sentence on Jamran in the grounds that it was a serious offence.Fazriel submitted that it was in the public interest that children are protected from sexual predators, especially within the same living area.“The court must send a clear message that such conduct will be met with severe consequences.“In light of the foregoing aggravating factors particularly the breach of trust, the vulnerability of the child victim, the serious nature of the sexual act, the absence of remorse, and the need for deterrence, the prosecution respectfully urges this Honourable Court to impose a stern and exemplary sentence in accordance with section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017,” he said. — Daily Express

Title: No whipping, 30 years’ jail for Filipino worker convicted of killing colleague in Kunak estate
Article:
TAWAU, Nov 20 — A palm oil transporter was sentenced to 30 years’ jail by the High Court after pleading guilty to murdering his female co-worker with a machete over personal dissatisfaction.
Judicial Commissioner Steve Ritikos ordered Roger Pasague Cullano, 54, to serve his sentence from the date of his arrest on June 14, 2025, and to be referred to the Malaysian Immigration Department upon completion of his prison term.
Roger was spared whipping due to his age. He had earlier pleaded guilty to murdering his fellow countrywoman, Abigail Diego Mandi, after the charge was read out by an interpreter in Visayan.
The father of two committed the offence in a bush area at Ample Land Tingkayu Estate, Kunak, between 9.30am and 10.15am on June 13, 2025.
The offence was framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which provides for the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years, with not less than 12 strokes of the cane if the death penalty is not imposed.
Based on the facts of the case, the victim was found by her son, Khasmer Diego Rhadzman, lying face down beneath a pile of oil palm fronds and bushes, with her trousers pulled down to her knees and her shirt raised to chest level. She also had several injuries to her head and face.
Earlier, Khasmer had gone to the location at about 10am to collect loose oil palm fruits after receiving a call from his mother. However, he could not find her and instead saw the accused nearby, covered in mud, with bloodstains on his cheek and holding a long machete.
During questioning after his arrest, Roger admitted to killing the victim because he was dissatisfied with her. He also admitted to attacking her with a machete, causing her death.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Mohd Fillany Siji prosecuted, while the accused was represented by lawyers Kamarudin Mohmad Chinki and Prem Elmer Ganasan.
In his submission for an appropriate sentence, Mohd Fillany said the accused had not only taken the life of a mother but had also caused trauma to her son, who discovered her body.
He said, considering the brutal nature of the murder and attack, as well as the absence of mitigating circumstances such as mental incapacity or grave and sudden provocation, the prosecution sought a prison term of between 30 and 35 years, taking into account the accused’s early guilty plea.
Meanwhile, Kamarudin, in his mitigation plea, urged the court to consider the accused’s age, educational background, social circumstances, family responsibilities and potential for rehabilitation when determining the sentence.
He said the guilty plea had saved court time and costs while sparing witnesses and the victim’s family from the emotional strain of giving evidence and undergoing cross-examination during a lengthy trial.
He added that the accused, now 54, was previously married, but his wife died in the Philippines several years ago. They have two children who are currently under the care of the accused’s family members. — Daily Express

Title: MPOB probes alleged palm oil blending, relabelling at Port Klang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 20 — The Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) is investigating a complaint alleging the blending of imported cooking oil with local supplies, and the relabelling of products for export as Malaysian products.
MPOB confirmed it received an official complaint on the matter, which is now under investigation to establish the validity of the allegations and examine whether any laws, regulations or licensing conditions within MPOB’s jurisdiction have been breached.
“The investigation includes a review of relevant records and documents, including data on the import, processing, storage and export of palm oil by the parties concerned.
“Cross-checks are also being carried out on blending activity records and shipping documents to identify any inconsistencies or discrepancies in the information,” it said in a statement today.
MPOB said the blending of palm oil and palm-based products is part of the industry’s processing activities, subject to compliance with licensing conditions, quality standards and the applicable legal provisions.
However, it said any act of providing false or misleading information about a product’s country of origin is a serious matter that must be addressed.
“The determination of the country of origin of export products must comply with the applicable Rules of Origin, including product-specific criteria under the relevant trade agreements.
“In this regard, the Preferential Certificate of Origin (PCO) is issued by the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) to enable exporters to enjoy reduced or exempted tariffs under free trade agreements (FTAs), subject to compliance with the stipulated conditions,” it said.
According to MPOB, the Non-Preferential Certificate of Origin (NPCO) is usually issued by chambers of commerce or trade associations appointed by MITI.
However, for exports to the United States, the issuance of the NPCO has been taken over entirely by MITI with effect from May 6, 2025, it said.
“The determination of origin must be made based on the origin criteria stipulated for the product and export destination concerned,” it said.
Should the investigation find evidence of a breach of the law or licensing conditions within its jurisdiction, appropriate action will be taken under the provisions of the Malaysian Palm Oil Board Act 1998 (Act 582) and related regulations, said MPOB.
A local news portal recently reported that a businessman lodged a complaint on Oct 19 over allegations that Indonesian refined, bleached and deodorised (RBD) palm olein was blended with Malaysian crude palm olein aboard tanker vessel MT Eunice at Port Klang on Sept 30. — Bernama

Title: Court of Appeal restores death sentence for man convicted of sodomising and murdering nine-month-old baby
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 20 — The Court of Appeal today described the actions of a man who sodomised and murdered a nine-month-old baby boy, who was under his wife’s care, as an act of extreme cruelty, inhuman and egregious violence against a helpless infant.
Court of Appeal judge Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz said the actions of the respondent, Mohamed Badruldin Mohamed, 41, demonstrated a blatant disregard for responsibility and a profound betrayal of the trust placed in his family.
“The victim was a nine-month-old boy entrusted by his mother to the respondent’s wife for childcare while she was at work. The respondent abused the trust and opportunity afforded to him, subjecting the victim to abuse, including sodomy, before ultimately causing his death by smothering, which obstructed his airways.
“A clear message must be sent to both the respondent and society at large that such crimes are utterly abhorrent, and the only appropriate ultimate penalty is the death sentence.
“Consequently, the prosecution’s appeal is allowed. The sentence of 30 years’ imprisonment and 12 strokes of the cane imposed by the High Court is set aside and replaced with the death sentence by hanging for the murder offence under Section 302 of the Penal Code,” she said when delivering the court’s decision.
The appeal was heard by a panel comprising Judge Datuk Azman Abdullah, who chaired the proceedings, and Judge Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid.
In the judgment, Hayatul Akmal said the sentence imposed by the Shah Alam High Court was inadequate.
“We have referred to the post-mortem report, which clearly documented injuries and bruising to the victim’s anus and lips, with the findings consistent with the cause of death, namely smothering. These injuries illustrate the cruelty and extraordinary pain that an innocent infant was forced to endure.
“A chemist also confirmed that the respondent’s sperm DNA was found in anal and rectal swabs taken from the victim. These findings indicate that the infant boy was sodomised by the respondent, the very person entrusted with ensuring his safety,” she said.
She further said the High Court judge had failed to provide reasonable justification for the sentence imposed.
“The High Court judge placed excessive weight on the respondent’s mitigating factors, namely his desire to reintegrate into society and become a better father, thereby sidelining the gravity of the crime committed against an innocent infant.
“In our view, the High Court judge overlooked the heinous nature of the offence, the substantive law and the magnitude of the crime. The failure to recognise its gravity necessitates our intervention to uphold substantive justice and correct a miscarriage of justice,” she said.
The prosecution appealed against the Shah Alam High Court’s decision on Nov 21, 2025, which sentenced Mohamed Badruldin to 30 years’ imprisonment and 12 strokes of the cane after he pleaded guilty to murdering the infant at a residential unit in the Lembah Subang People’s Housing Project (PPR), Ara Damansara, between 8am and 3.30pm on April 27, 2021.
Apart from the murder charge, Mohamed Badruldin was also charged with committing carnal intercourse against the order of nature with the same victim, an offence under Section 377C of the Penal Code.
The offence was committed between 11am and noon on the same day at the same location. The High Court sentenced him to 10 years’ imprisonment and one stroke of the cane, with the prison term to run concurrently with the sentence for murder.
However, the prosecution did not appeal against the sentence for the sodomy offence.
At today’s proceedings, the prosecution was represented by Deputy Public Prosecutor Norshazwani Ishak, while Mohamed Badruldin was represented by lawyers Datuk Mohtarudin Baki and Jayananda Rao. — Bernama

Title: Perlis NGO director arrested at KLIA2 over alleged RM85,468 criminal breach of trust
Article:
KANGAR, Nov 20 — The director of a non-governmental organisation (NGO) based here was arrested by police on suspicion of committing criminal breach of trust involving funds belonging to the organisation amounting to RM85,468 in Sepang, Selangor today.
Perlis Police Chief DCP Hamzah Hashim said the 31-year-old man was detained by police from the Commercial Crime Investigation Department, Perlis Contingent Police Headquarters, at the domestic arrival gate of the Kuala Lumpur International Airport 2 (KLIA2) at 11.05am today following information and intelligence.
“At the time of the arrest, the suspect was travelling from Sabah to Kuala Lumpur. The amount of RM85,468 is believed to involve 32 transactions into the suspect’s personal account over the period between 2 March 2026 and 20 July 2026,” he said in a statement today.
Hamzah said the case is being investigated under Section 409 of the Penal Code, while a remand application for the man to assist in the investigation will be made tomorrow.
He said police will not compromise on any form of criminal breach of trust involving the abuse of position, power, and trust given, adding that firm action will be taken against any party found involved in unlawful activities regardless of the individual’s position or status. — Bernama

Title: Nuclear plant in Selangor? State scouting coast from Kuala Langat to Sabak Bernam, but nothing final yet
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 20 — Selangor is looking at sites along its coastline, from Kuala Langat to Sabak Bernam, for a proposed nuclear power plant, Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said today.
Amirudin was responding to Pakatan Harapan assemblyman for Kota Damansara Muhammad Izuan Ahmad Kasim, who asked about the state’s nuclear energy plans, including the proposed allocation and potential sites, at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly sitting here.
“Worldwide Holdings Bhd has established a special committee to look into the requirements and preliminary preparations,” he was quoted as saying by The Star.
“At the same time, the state government is studying several measures to formulate policies in line with the Federal Government’s direction,” he added.
Amirudin said coastal areas were being considered because nuclear power plants need access to seawater for cooling and other operational needs.
Bernama reported that he stressed the area was still under review and had not been finalised as the site for a nuclear power plant.
Bernama also reported that Worldwide Holdings Berhad, a state-owned subsidiary, had formed a committee and a special task force, with the aim of accelerating physical development works from 2030.
Amirudin said the Selangor Nuclear Council, made up of academics and industry players, was drawing up a roadmap to prepare the state for developing a nuclear industry, The Star reported.
He said the state was also implementing a talent development framework for 2025 to 2030 to build local expertise in nuclear technology, according to Bernama.
The framework includes sponsoring students to study nuclear engineering at Harbin Engineering University and Tsinghua University in China, Bernama reported.
“Three students were sent last September to pursue their studies until 2029, and the state government plans to send another 22 students in 2027, bringing the total to 25,” he was quoted as saying by Bernama.
The Star reported that the students were recipients of RM3.7 million in scholarships from China General Nuclear for degree, master’s and PhD programmes.
Amirudin said the state was prepared to support their studies up to doctoral level, according to The Star.
He said the state is also studying nuclear energy development models adopted by countries including China, France and Türkiye.
Selangor is also looking at Kazakhstan’s model, which draws on expertise from France, China, Russia and Türkiye.

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB acknowledges mistakes, reaffirms loyalty to Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 20 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim today pledged allegiance to Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, and vowed to uphold the sovereignty of the state’s royal institution, abide by the Negeri Sembilan State Constitution 1959 and comply with all decisions of the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU).
Ismail said the undertaking reaffirmed his recognition of Tuanku Muhriz as the state’s legitimate Ruler and his commitment to safeguarding His Royal Highness’s sovereignty, powers, rights and privileges.
He also confirmed that a proclamation dated April 19 was invalid, had no legal effect, and would not be gazetted.
“Alhamdulillah, I have received the consent of Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir to continue carrying out my duties as Menteri Besar. I therefore affirm unequivocally that Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir remains the legitimate Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.
“I will neither undertake nor permit any state assemblyman, department, agency or state government official to commit any act that diminishes, removes, overrides or undermines His Royal Highness’s sovereignty, position, prerogatives, powers, rights or privileges,” he told a press conference at the Menteri Besar’s official residence here today.
Ismail also pledged that neither he nor the state government would support or facilitate any attempt to challenge Tuanku Muhriz’s position, recognise another individual as Yang Dipertuan Besar or revive the proclamation.
He further acknowledged DKU decisions dated July 31, Aug 20, Sept 13, Sept 18 and Nov 4, including the recognition of Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari as Undang Luak Sungai Ujong, Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid as Undang Luak Rembau and Datuk Azrin Khairi as Undang Luak Jelebu.
Ismail also accepted that Datuk Mubarak Thahak @ Dohak and Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad had ceased to hold the positions of Undang Luak Sungai Ujong and Undang Luak Jelebu, respectively, in accordance with the customs of their respective luak.
He said Abdul Rahim Yassin, in the other hand, had never been validly appointed Undang Luak Rembau under the prescribed customs, nor had his appointment been formalised through the required traditional installation ceremony.
“Therefore, none of the individuals mentioned has the legal authority to exercise any powers under Article 10 of the Law and Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 959,” he said.
Ismail also acknowledged that Datuk Shahbandar Datuk Seri Badarudin Abdul Khalid had been removed from his position in accordance with the customs of Luak Sungai Ujong.
In a related development, he said he had written to Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal Tan Sri Syed Danial Syed Ahmad to withdraw a letter dated Sept 17.
He also pledged to ensure that the revocation of a State Executive Council decision dated Sept 15 would be recorded in the minutes of its next meeting.
“I reiterate this oath of allegiance, witnessed by the Quran, that I solemnly swear to respect and pledge loyalty to Tuanku Muhriz and the royal institution, protect and preserve the sovereignty of the state constitution, and recognise the authority vested in the DKU.
“Finally, I sign this undertaking with full understanding of its contents and implications. I am not acting under any coercion, threat or undue influence,” he said.
Ismail said the undertaking reflected his acknowledgement of mistakes made while leading the state administration and his responsibility to ensure that all members of the state government continued to respect and remain loyal to Tuanku Muhriz, the royal institution and the DKU. — Bernama

Title: Putrajaya’s plan for Rohingya refugees: Train 10,000 in skills, resettle them in Türkiye
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 20 — The Cabinet has agreed to resettle 10,000 Rohingya refugees from Malaysia in Türkiye through a structured skills training programme, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today.
Zahid, who chairs the Cabinet Committee on Foreign Workers, said he proposed the plan after his recent official working visit to Türkiye, as part of efforts to address the Rohingya refugee situation in a more coordinated, effective and humane manner.
“In addressing the situation of refugees, we must uphold our immigration laws while giving due consideration to humanitarian concerns,” he said in a press statement.
He welcomed Türkiye’s agreement to receive the refugees, calling it an important step towards a long-term solution to an issue that he said “has long posed challenges for migration management and national security”.
Zahid said the refugees would undergo a Technical and Vocational Education and Training programme lasting three to six months, focusing on practical skills in demand among employers across various industries in Türkiye.
He said participants would then be better equipped to find work and contribute to Türkiye’s economy, subject to the country’s rules and regulations.
Zahid said Putrajaya would work with Turkish authorities, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and relevant agencies to coordinate participant selection, training, documentation and resettlement.
“Implementation will take into account industry needs, the consent of the individuals concerned and applicable international rules,” he said.
He said the initiative was in line with the principles guiding UNHCR in seeking lasting solutions for refugees, including resettlement in a third country, with due regard for their safety, protection and dignity.
“Our cooperation with Türkiye could serve as a model for how countries can work together to manage refugee resettlement in an orderly, sustainable and dignified manner,” he said.
Malaysia hosted about 126,000 Rohingya registered with UNHCR as of the end of February, Bernama reported, citing from UNHCR figures.
In July, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Myanmar had agreed to take 5,000 Rohingya asylum seekers from Malaysia while UNHCR said it did not support returns to Myanmar given the ongoing conflict there.

Title: Anwar says pressure won’t change his support for Xi Jinping or China ties
Article:
SHENZHEN, Nov 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he had no regrets about giving his full support to Chinese President Xi Jinping despite various pressures, reaffirming Malaysia’s commitment to strengthening bilateral relations with China.
Anwar said his support was based on his confidence in Xi’s leadership, particularly his ability to bring major world powers together and foster peace amid geopolitical uncertainties.
“That is why I don’t regret at all my decision to give full support to you as a great leader of the world and to establish strong bilateral relations notwithstanding whatever pressures that we have,” he said during his welcoming remarks at a bilateral meeting with Xi at the Qilin Villa State Guest House here today.
Anwar also commended Xi for bringing together United States President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, describing it as an achievement few world leaders could accomplish.
“That takes only President Xi; I don’t know anyone else who could do that. And congratulations, because it means a lot. People like us in the developing countries will look to someone who has that wisdom and courage to be able to pull these three together,” he said.
The Prime Minister also praised China’s successful hosting of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Week, saying Malaysia was impressed by the scale of its infrastructure and the overall organisation of the event, including the hospitality extended to delegates.
“First, we see the massive, impressive infrastructure. But this time, President, under your leadership, the whole arrangement, from the very top to ... even the butler at the hotel,” he said.
He said the Malaysian delegation had expressed admiration for the arrangements and hoped to emulate some of China’s approaches in Malaysia.
Anwar said his visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou in September, during which he also held discussions with Chinese Premier Li Qiang, had further strengthened bilateral ties, with both countries subsequently agreeing to expand cooperation in several areas. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says Xi’s interest in Malaysia Madani reflects China’s openness to deeper cultural ties
Article:
SHENZHEN, Nov 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he was struck by Chinese President Xi Jinping’s keen interest in the Malaysia Madani concept and efforts to deepen understanding between Islamic and Confucian civilisations, describing such attention from the leader of a major power as rare in bilateral relations.
Anwar said Xi’s attention to these matters was among the highlights of their bilateral meeting today, reflecting China’s openness to Malaysia’s perspectives on Madani and inter-civilisational cooperation.
“I find this quite remarkable. It is rare in bilateral relations to see the president of a major power take such a keen interest in our views on Madani and civilisational cooperation,” he told Malaysian journalists after meeting Xi at the Qilin Villa State Guest House here today.
Anwar said Xi had previously expressed interest in strengthening cooperation in these areas through dialogue, research and initiatives to promote mutual understanding between Islamic and Confucian civilisations.
He said Malaysia would fully support these efforts, including through universities and educational institutions, to expand research and understanding of Islamic civilisation, Chinese culture and other civilisations.
The Prime Minister described the initiative as unusual, particularly given China’s position as a major non-Muslim country willing to respect Malaysia’s perspectives and pursue a deeper understanding of Islamic civilisation.
He said the cooperation could also be further strengthened through educational partnerships, academic exchanges and increased tourism between the two countries.
Such efforts, he added, were important in fostering mutual understanding, respect and closer ties among people of different cultural and religious backgrounds. — Bernama

Title: Not so fast: Negeri Sembilan palace says Ismail Lasim must show majority support, not just deny resigning as MB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 20 — The Negeri Sembilan Palace today said Datuk Ismail Lasim must show that he still commands majority support in the state assembly and submit a list of state executive councillors, after he denied resigning as menteri besar.
The palace was responding after Ismail told reporters this morning that Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir had instructed him to carry on, following reports that he had resigned in a letter dated November 16.
“Since he himself stated that he did not resign, it is inaccurate and not based on fact to say that the palace wants him to remain as menteri besar,” the Negeri Sembilan Comptroller of the Royal Household said in a statement.
“The palace will fully comply with conventions and constitutional provisions, and Datuk Ismail Lasim must show that he still has the support of the majority of state assembly members,” it added.
The palace said Ismail told Tuanku Muhriz at this morning’s audience, which the Undangs also attended, that he neither submitted the letter nor consented to its submission, and had said the same at a press conference today.
It reiterated that a menteri besar’s resignation takes effect only if the ruler consents, and that the palace had not verified the letter.
The palace said Ismail must also submit a list of state executive council members for Tuanku Muhriz’s consideration.
It said the date of the state assembly sitting and the tabling of the state budget would be fixed only after these matters were settled, in accordance with the state constitution.
Tuanku Muhriz hoped the matter could be resolved swiftly for the benefit of the people of Negeri Sembilan, the palace said.
Barisan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir announced on November 16 that Ismail had resigned in a letter dated that same day.
A day later, the palace said that the resignation would take effect only with the Ruler’s consent, while the state secretary said on November 18 that his office had received no official notification.
The episode follows a royal dispute in September, when Tuanku Muhriz revoked the appointments of 10 state executive councillors who had backed claims that his removal as ruler was legitimate.
On November 10, Ismail and the 10 councillors told the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal that the state government had withdrawn an earlier letter sent to the Conference of Rulers.
Ismail was sworn in as menteri besar on August 2.

Title: Maju Holdings boss, wife to face 21-day trial over RM458.5m CBT, money laundering charges from July 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 20 — The Sessions Court today fixed 21 days between July and October next year for the trial of criminal breach of trust (CBT) and money laundering cases involving Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd director Tan Sri Abu Sahid Mohamed and his wife, Puan Sri Noor Azrina Mohd Azmi.
Judge Suzana Hussin set the dates for July 21 to 23; August 18 to 20 and 27; September 6 to 9, 20, 21 and 24; and October 4 to 7 and 11 to 13, 2027.
At today’s mention, deputy public prosecutor Esther Jacyntha handed the defence three volumes of documents, completing the document discovery process. The court subsequently fixed March 22, 2027 for the next mention.
Abu Sahid faces five charges of misappropriating more than RM458.5 million in company funds entrusted to him, involving bank accounts in Taman Tunku and Taman Serdang Perdana between May 3, 2016 and October 21, 2019.
The charges were framed under Section 409 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years, caning and a fine upon conviction.
He also faces 10 charges of transferring proceeds from unlawful activities amounting to RM116,449,536.12 from his accounts to five individuals and four construction companies.
In three additional money laundering charges, Abu Sahid is alleged to have disposed of proceeds from unlawful activities totalling RM22,802,612.86 by withdrawing cash through 15 cheques from his account at the same bank between May 4, 2016 and September 19, 2018.
Noor Azrina, meanwhile, was charged with receiving proceeds from unlawful activities amounting to RM67.14 million through her bank account from Abu Sahid’s account.
The offence was allegedly committed at a bank in Bukit Tunku between March 6 and November 27, 2017.
Abu Sahid’s three money laundering charges and Noor Azrina’s charge were brought under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 and are punishable under Section 4(1) of the same Act.
A conviction under the section carries a maximum prison term of 15 years and a fine of not less than five times the amount of the proceeds of unlawful activity or RM5 million, whichever is higher. — Bernama

Title: Tawau house fire claims lives of two siblings aged 10 and 13
Article:
TAWAU, Nov 20 — Two siblings aged 10 and 13 were killed in a fire that destroyed a double-storey terrace house at Taman Ria here on Friday.
The victims, a 10-year-old girl with autism and disabilities and her 13-year-old brother, were found dead in an upstairs bedroom.
Four other occupants managed to escape before firefighters arrived.
Tawau Fire and Rescue Station chief Deputy Fire Superintendent II Jemishin Ujin said the department received an emergency call at 6.13am, with the first fire engine arriving nine minutes later.
“Two victims were still trapped inside the house when firefighters arrived, prompting an immediate rescue operation.
However, both were found dead at 6.43am and their bodies were later handed over to police,” he said in a statement.
Jemishin said the fire destroyed about 70 per cent of the building.
A total of 16 firefighters brought the blaze under control by 7.07am. The operation ended at 9.06am after the scene was declared safe, he said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Johor data centres’ water usage is just over 1pc of state’s treated water production, says exco
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 20 — The 19 data centres in Johor consume 21.277 million litres per day (MLD) of treated water, which makes up only 1.05 per cent of the state’s total treated water production, said State Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh.
He explained that the data centres had initially requested 73.088 MLD of water, but a lower volume of 21.277 MLD was approved instead, which makes up 3.35 per cent of the industrial sector’s total water consumption.
To put the figures into perspective, Mohamad Fazli said Johor produces an average of 2,034 MLD of treated water, of which 904 MLD is used for domestic purposes and 635 MLD by industries.
“In addition, nine of the 19 operational data centres make use of efficient cooling systems capable of operating with zero water consumption.
“Another 11 data centres consume less than 1 MLD of water, while the remainder consume between 1 and 4.172 MLD.
“Despite the data centres’ low water usage, making up only a small fraction of the state’s total treated water production, the state government will ensure that it does not compromise the needs of domestic consumers in the future,” he said at the Johor state legislative assembly in Kota Iskandar here today.
Mohamad Fazli, who is also the Bukit Pasir assemblyman, was responding to questions on water and other utilities raised by Baharudin Mohamed Taib (BN-Permas), Datuk Pandak Ahmad (BN-Kota Iskandar) and R. Kumaran (BN-Bukit Batu).
He pointed out that Johor was the first state to establish the Johor Data Centre Development Coordination Committee (JPPPDNJ), in 2024.
“Through the JPPPDNJ, water and electricity supply requirements are assessed in an integrated manner with the Johor Water Regulatory Body (BAKAJ), Ranhill SAJ (RSAJ), Johor Special Water (JSW) and Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB),” he said, adding that operators with high water-consumption requirements had been asked to use alternative water sources via JSW, including treated wastewater from sewage treatment plants, in accordance with industrial needs.
On the decline in water levels at six dams, Mohamad Fazli attributed the situation to the prolonged drought and the El Niño phenomenon, which is expected to have its peak impact through March 2027.
He explained that the 19 data centres receive their supply from the Semangar and Sungai Johor water treatment plants, both of which draw raw water from Sungai Johor.
“The six dams under monitoring are the Machap, Lebam, Gunung Pulai 2, Pontian Kechil, Upper Layang and Lower Layang dams,” he said, pointing out that the Machap and Lebam dams do not supply water to any data centres.

Title: Anwar meets Xi for fourth bilateral talks as Malaysia-China ties deepen
Article:
SHENZHEN, Nov 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today held a bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, reaffirming close diplomatic ties between Malaysia and China.
The 20-minute meeting was held at Qilin Villa State Guest House and is the fourth between Anwar and Xi, reflecting continued high-level engagements as Malaysia and China strengthen their strategic partnership.
Their first bilateral meeting was held on November 7, 2024, in Beijing, China, followed by the second on April 16, 2025, in Putrajaya.
The third meeting took place on September 2, 2025, in Beijing, China.
Anwar is in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) Economic Leaders’ Week 2026, which brings together leaders from member economies to discuss regional economic cooperation, trade, connectivity and emerging challenges. — Bernama

Title: Johor vows tougher action as school bullying cases climb past 1,000 a year
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 20 — The Johor state government will take more serious steps on the safety and well-being of students in schools, following a concerning number of recent bullying cases.
State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said schools must be kept safe, as bullying has become a primary concern for students, parents, educators and the general public.
He said official statistics from the Education Ministry showed an upward trend in bullying cases nationwide, rising from 6,528 cases in 2023 to 7,681 cases in 2024.
“In Johor, 984 bullying cases were recorded in 2023, increasing to 1,080 cases in 2024. As of September this year, there were 773 cases recorded.
“The statistics show an upward trend, with the number of cases remaining high.
“In light of this, out-of-the-ordinary measures are required to ensure that the issue of safety in schools is addressed more effectively,” he said at the Johor state legislative assembly in Kota Iskandar here today.
Dr Muhammad Naqib was responding to questions from assemblymen Datuk Zulkurnain Kamisan (BN-Sri Medan), Selamat Takim (BN-Sungai Balang) and Chu Poh Yee (PH-Mengkibol), who asked about student disciplinary issues, the death of a student in Yong Peng and general school safety.
Citing research findings, the Panti assemblyman said there were three key areas that must be addressed at the same time to tackle bullying in schools.
He said the three areas were illicit substance and drug abuse, bullying, and mental health issues among students.
“In order to address this issue at the federal level, the Education Ministry has implemented various proactive measures, including a dedicated platform that allows students to anonymously report any wrongdoing in confidence.
“This includes the ministry’s 1:3:7 reporting and action timeline procedure to ensure proper handling regarding student discipline and safety incidents across schools.
“In addition, there is also a need for the installation of closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras in schools,” he said, adding that the Anti-Bullying Act 2026 (Act 876) represented the federal government’s latest legislative measure to streamline and strengthen efforts to combat bullying in educational premises.
At the state level, Dr Muhammad Naqib said the Johor government, together with state and district education agencies, had launched the Johor Safe School Campaign through the J-Safe initiative.
“The J-Safe initiative comprises two main components: ‘J-Safe Action’, a digital guidance instrument for school management, and the J-Safe Smart Youth Movement, which empowers students to act as strategic partners in fostering a safe school culture.
“The Johor Student Character Programme (KrMJ) has also been recommended to cultivate positive values in every child.
“This is in addition to other programmes involving the State Education Department (JPN), the District Education Office (PPD), schools, the police, the National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK), counsellors and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) in recommending solutions,” he said.

Title: No plans to resume use of the automatic number plate recognition system for now, says Penang exco
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 20 — Penang has no immediate plans to resume using its automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) system, state executive councillor H’ng Mooi Lye said today.
However, the Penang local government and town and country planning committee chairman said that doesn’t mean they will no longer use the system in the future.
“There are many uses to the ANPR, not only for enforcement uses so if we were to start using it again, it would most probably be for data collection,” he said in a press conference at his office today.
However, H’ng said there is no set date for when both city councils will resume using the system.
“We will definitely announce to the public if we resume using the system, even if it’s for parking management and data collection,” he said.
He stressed that the state has no intention to use ANPR for enforcement purposes and had previously cancelled the summonses issued through the system.
He said during the recent state legislative assembly early this month, there was a question on whether both councils would relaunch the system and he had replied yes.
“That was misunderstood as that we will be using the system for enforcement, which is not true,” he said, referring to a social media post by a Chinese vernacular newspaper that had stated parking enforcement using ANPR would resume.
“People are asking why the state government stopped using ANPR for enforcement and is now suddenly going to relaunch it for enforcement,” he said.
He explained that the system can be used to help councils monitor parking bay use and manage parking facilities more effectively.
“The roadside scans could help the Penang Island City Council (MBPP), the Seberang Perai City Council (MBSP) and the state government measure compliance with parking rules and identify areas where roadside parking was common,”
“Penang has very narrow streets and many vehicles so this system will be helpful to capture data,” he said.
He added that the data could help the authorities decide which areas needed attention and what kind of development would be suitable there.
He said the data could also be analysed using artificial intelligence to assess whether a multi-storey car park was suitable and how many floors and parking bays it should have.
H’ng pointed out that ANPR was already widely used, citing the Penang International Airport car park and the JustGo toll payment system as examples.
“So we can use this system for automated entry and exit at council car parks,” he said.
He said the cameras could read plates as vehicles entered an unattended car park, send the numbers to the main system and detect whether a vehicle was leaving without payment.
“If we use ANPR again, we will engage with the public and make an announcement,” he said, adding that this would apply even if a council installed it at one of its own car parks.
ANPR uses smart cameras to scan and read vehicle registration plates automatically.
The vendor introduced the system under an existing service contract to help both councils check whether motorists using marked bays had paid for parking, making monitoring more systematic and reducing reliance on manual checks by enforcement officers.
H’ng said the state had taken note of public concerns, including how the system treated a vehicle occupying a parking bay while the driver was still inside.
“I understand that enforcement using this technology can cause dissatisfaction and concern among motorists, particularly if there is confusion over how detection and enforcement are carried out,” he said.
He said the state is now reviewing how ANPR could be used with both councils and the vendor, taking into account conditions on the ground and the interests of motorists.
“We want to make sure that the way it is implemented is suitable, clear and takes into account the actual conditions on the ground and the interests of parking users,” H’ng said.

Title: Tuanku Muhriz decrees Ismail Lasim to stay on as Negeri Sembilan MB; Ismail says he never submitted resignation letter
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 20 — Datuk Ismail Lasim will remain Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar on the decree of Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, amid controversy over a purported resignation letter that Ismail denied submitting or authorising.
Ismail said Tuanku Muhriz had instructed him to continue carrying out his duties to ensure continuity in the state administration.
Confirming the matter, Ismail pledged to discharge his duties and responsibilities with full dedication.
“I wish to clarify reports concerning a letter of resignation as Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar dated Nov 16. I neither submitted nor consented to the submission of the letter to Tuanku Muhriz,” he told reporters at the Menteri Besar’s official residence here today.
Ismail arrived at Istana Hinggap here at 10.17 am for an audience with Tuanku Muhriz amid the political turmoil in the state.
Also present at the palace were Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid, Undang Luak Sungai Ujong Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari and Undang Luak Jelebu Datuk Azrin Khairi.
Last Monday, Ismail, who is also Juasseh assemblyman, was reported to have resigned as Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar, a post he was sworn into on Aug 2.
The Negeri Sembilan Palace said on Tuesday that a Menteri Besar’s resignation would only take effect upon receiving Tuanku Muhriz’s consent, in accordance with the Law and Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959.
On the same day, Tuanku Muhriz granted Ismail an audience, with the meeting lasting from about 5 pm to 6.30 pm. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan impasse: Ismail Lasim granted audience with Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 20 — Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim arrived at Istana Hinggap here at 10.17 am today for an audience with the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, amid the administrative impasse in the state.
Earlier, Tuanku Muhriz arrived at the palace at about 9.30 am, followed by three Undang Luak (traditional chieftains) of Negeri Sembilan.
They were Rembau Undang Luak Datuk Sedia Raja Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid, Sungai Ujong Undang Luak Datuk Klana Petra Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari and Jelebu Undang Luak Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi.
Ismail, who is also the Juasseh state assemblyman, is understood to have sought the audience to discuss the impasse.
Last Monday, Barisan Nasional announced that Ismail, 67, has resigned as Menteri Besar. He was sworn in on Aug 2.
The following day, the Negeri Sembilan palace said that the Menteri Besar’s resignation would only take effect upon receiving the consent of Tuanku Muhriz, in accordance with the Negeri Sembilan State Constitution 1959.
On the same day, Tuanku Muhriz was reported to have granted an audience to Ismail from 5 pm to 6.30 pm. — Bernama

Title: Declassified minutes show Hannah Yeoh objected to Najib house arrest, says Lim Guan Eng
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 20 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng today defended Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh over her role in the pardon process involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, saying she had upheld the party’s opposition to Najib’s house arrest proposal during a Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting.
Lim said declassified minutes from the September 18, 2026 Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting showed that Yeoh had clearly stated her objections to the move during proceedings chaired by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
He said that despite her objections, Yeoh had complied with a royal decree requiring her to sign the pardon proclamation.
“Hannah discharged her duty not only as a DAP leader but also her ministerial responsibility professing full loyalty to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong,” Lim said in a statement today.
The Bagan MP also cited Yeoh’s role in announcing the government’s decision to renew the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall’s (KLSCAH) lease for 99 years, with a nominal land premium of RM1,000 instead of the estimated RM4.67 million.
According to Lim, Yeoh had faced criticism from groups and individuals seeking to turn the matter into a racial issue.
He said Yeoh had maintained that the reduction in the land premium was justified because KLSCAH holds heritage status and cannot be commercially developed.
Lim added that Malaysia needed leaders and ministers who make decisions based on the merits of each case rather than on “inflammatory sentiments and provocative rhetoric”.

Title: Residents’ association cannot force homeowners to become members, Shah Alam court rules
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 20 — A residents’ association cannot automatically make homeowners its members or compel them to pay security fees backdated over previous years, the Sessions Court here has ruled, Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported.
Judge Zuhrina Nor Hakim allowed a civil suit filed by homeowner Abdul Farid Abdul Kadir against Persatuan Penduduk Jalan Hijau Pelangi and its chairman, Saaidal Razalli Azzuhri, and awarded him RM20,000 in damages.
In her decision on Monday, the judge also threw out the association’s and its chairman’s counterclaim in full.
The case centred on the association’s position that Abdul Farid was automatically a member and owed security charges going back to 2013.
Abdul Farid maintained that he had never applied for membership. He argued that under the association’s constitution, a homeowner must apply to become a member, and membership cannot simply be imposed.
He also challenged the demand for backdated security payments covering a period when he was living abroad and not occupying the house.
According to his statement of claim, Abdul Farid returned to Malaysia in July 2020 and applied to join the association, offering RM1,410 for membership and security services.
The association rejected his application and insisted that he first clear the charges that had built up over the previous years.
The dispute also involved access arrangements at the Cahaya SPK housing development in Shah Alam.
Abdul Farid claimed that residents who did not pay the security charges had to stop their vehicles and lift the boom gate themselves, even when guards were on duty.
